options: Rigidity occurs in all the muscles of the body
Increase in the rate of discharge of the γ efferent neuron
Increased excitability of the motor neuron pool
Decerebration produces no phenomenon akin to spinal shock
records.explanation: Decerebrate posturing predominantly extends limbs through disordered brainstem motor control. Saying all muscles become uniformly rigid is an oversimplification, and the complete alternatives need review.

records.question: Which of the following is true for decorticate rigidity?
options: It is produced by the removal of cerebral cortex and basal ganglia
Flexion of lower limbs and extension of upper limbs occurs
It is characterized by flexion of upper limbs and extension of lower limbs
records.explanation: Decorticate posturing classically flexes the upper limbs and extends the lower limbs, reflecting loss of descending control above the red-nucleus level.

records.question: Acid Citrate Dextrose (ACD), used to store blood, preserves the RBCs for a period of 21 days. The storage period when adding phosphate alone and when adding adenine and phosphate together to ACD would respectively be?
records.explanation: Conventional CPD-preserved red cells have a twenty-one-day shelf life, while CPDA-1 permits thirty-five days. Storage specifications depend on the collection system and regulatory standard.

records.question: Functional residual capacity is:
options: Volume that remains after forced expiration
records.explanation: Functional residual capacity is the volume remaining after normal expiration and equals expiratory reserve volume plus residual volume.

records.question: Lesion in the medial lemniscus at the level of pons causes which of the following?
options: Pain and temperature loss in the same side
Pain and temperature loss in the opposite side
Loss of tactile and proprioception on the same side
Loss of tactile and proprioception on the opposite side
records.explanation: At pontine level the medial lemniscus carries already-crossed dorsal-column sensory information. Injury causes contralateral loss of vibration, discriminative touch and proprioception below the lesion.

records.question: Which neurotransmitter is responsible for anterograde dilation of the small intestine?
records.explanation: VIP contributes inhibitory enteric signalling and smooth-muscle relaxation ahead of a propagating intestinal contraction. Nitric oxide is another important inhibitory transmitter.

records.question: Reflex responsible for tachycardia during right atrial distension is:
records.explanation: Increased venous return stretches atrial receptors and can increase heart rate through the Bainbridge reflex, with interaction from other cardiovascular reflexes.

records.question: Testosterone production is mainly contributed by _________
records.explanation: LH stimulates Leydig cells to synthesise testosterone. Sertoli cells instead support spermatogenesis and produce factors including inhibin B.

records.question: The following appearance in IVP is caused by:
records.explanation: A ureterocele is cystic dilatation of the distal ureter and can produce a cobra-head appearance on contrast imaging. The IVP image must confirm that sign.

records.question: What is the function of tubuloglomerular feedback?
records.explanation: Macula-densa sensing of distal sodium-chloride delivery adjusts afferent tone and renin signalling, helping regulate single-nephron filtration.

records.question: Based on the agglutination test shown below, what is the blood group?
records.explanation: Agglutination with anti-A, anti-B and anti-D reagents determines forward ABO and RhD typing. The actual reaction pattern is required to verify O positive.

records.question: Which of the following neurons predominantly fire during forceful expiration?
records.explanation: Ventral respiratory-group networks recruit expiratory motor output during active or forceful expiration. Quiet expiration is largely passive.

records.question: ADH acts through which aquaporin channel?
records.explanation: V2-receptor signalling promotes aquaporin-2 insertion into collecting-duct principal-cell apical membranes, increasing water reabsorption.

records.question: Which of the following has the least conduction velocity?
records.explanation: Postganglionic sympathetic fibres are predominantly small unmyelinated C fibres, which conduct more slowly than larger myelinated motor or sensory fibres.

records.question: Which part of the liver stores vitamin A?
records.explanation: Hepatic stellate, or Ito, cells store vitamin A in lipid droplets. Activation during liver injury can shift them toward a fibrogenic phenotype.

records.question: Liver synthesizes all of the following except:
records.explanation: Plasma cells produce immunoglobulins. The liver synthesises many other plasma proteins, including albumin and numerous coagulation factors.

records.question: Which of the following ions is involved in peripheral oxygen sensing chemoreceptors?
records.explanation: Hypoxia inhibits oxygen-sensitive potassium currents in carotid-body glomus cells, promoting depolarisation, calcium entry and transmitter release.

records.question: Brown sequard syndrome is characterized by ___________
options: Fine touch lost on the opposite side
Pain and temperature lost on the same side
Pain and temperature loss on the opposite side
Only pain lost on the same side
records.explanation: Spinothalamic fibres cross near their entry level, so cord hemisection produces contralateral pain-temperature loss below the lesion alongside ipsilateral dorsal-column and motor deficits.

records.question: Match the following intracranial bleed: 1. Epidural hematoma i. 2. Subdural hematoma ii. 3. Subarchniod Haemorrhage iii. 4. Intracerebral haemmorrhage iv.
records.explanation: Epidural bleeding lies between skull and dura, subdural bleeding between dura and arachnoid, and subarachnoid bleeding within the CSF-containing subarachnoid space. Intraparenchymal bleeding occurs within brain tissue.

records.question: Which of the following investigations is shown in the radiograph?
records.explanation: A barium meal outlines upper gastrointestinal anatomy. The radiograph's contrast location and timing are needed to distinguish it from swallow, follow-through or other studies.

records.question: What is the best imaging study for the earliest diagnosis of cerebral infarct?
records.explanation: Diffusion-weighted MRI can detect restricted water diffusion early in acute cerebral ischaemia. Emergency imaging choice still depends on treatment timing and excluding haemorrhage without delay.

records.question: During evaluation of PUO, a patient’s chest X-ray is as seen below. What is your diagnosis?
records.explanation: Disseminated tuberculosis can produce diffuse fine nodules on chest imaging. Other causes of a miliary pattern exist, requiring clinical and microbiological correlation.

records.question: Identify the structure marked in the following MRI scan:
records.explanation: The cerebellum lies in the posterior fossa behind the brainstem and coordinates movement and balance. The actual label and imaging plane determine the marked structure.

records.question: Which of the following is a water soluble contrast?
records.explanation: Iohexol is a nonionic water-soluble iodinated contrast agent. Suitability and route depend on the examination, renal assessment and previous contrast reactions.

records.question: All of the following could be the cause of the following X-ray finding except:
records.explanation: Radiographic bowel-gas patterns reflect obstruction, ileus and other processes.

records.question: The type of knot seen in the image is?
records.explanation: A reef or square knot uses opposing throws to create a balanced knot. The image must show throw direction before distinguishing it from a granny knot.

records.question: What is the drug used for estrogen dependant breast cancer?
records.explanation: Tamoxifen modulates oestrogen receptors and antagonises oestrogen action in breast tissue. Treatment selection depends on receptor status and individual benefits and risks.

records.question: The commonest surgical approach to a retrosternal goitre is via?
records.explanation: Many retrosternal goitres can be removed through a cervical approach. Extent, ectopic supply, malignancy and mediastinal anatomy may require a different or combined approach.

records.question: An intern placed an intercostal drainage tube in a patient. Which of the following steps is incorrect?
options: Identified 5th intercostal space anterior to mid axillary line to place the tube
Inserted above the upper border of the rib
Insertion of the needle, which will be between your ribs on your back
records.explanation: Chest-drain insertion uses a deliberately selected safe anatomical site and technique, avoiding neurovascular structures and underlying organs. A generic posterior intercostal instruction is insufficient and potentially unsafe.

records.question: What is the size of the given blade used for incision and drainage of a superficial abscess?
records.explanation: A number-eleven blade has a pointed tip suited to selected stab incisions. The photographed blade must be confirmed before assigning its number.

records.question: A 40-year-old patient presents to the emergency department following a road traffic accident. The radiograph of his pelvis is shown below. What is the most likely diagnosis?
records.explanation: Posterior dislocation commonly follows dashboard-type trauma and may present with a shortened internally rotated limb. Radiographs confirm direction and associated fracture before urgent management.

records.question: A 12-year-old boy presents with a gradually progressing swelling and pain for 6 months over the upper tibia. His radiographic image is shown below. The most likely diagnosis is:
records.explanation: A Brodie abscess is a localised subacute osteomyelitic lesion, often metaphyseal with surrounding sclerosis. The radiograph is required to distinguish tumour and other lesions.

records.question: In a blast injury, which of the following organs is least vulnerable to the blast wave?
records.explanation: Gas-containing organs are particularly vulnerable to primary blast pressure waves. Solid liver tissue is relatively less susceptible to that mechanism, although other blast-related forces can still injure it.

records.question: Which of the following fractures is most prone to non-union?
records.explanation: The proximal scaphoid has vulnerable retrograde blood supply, increasing risks of avascular necrosis and nonunion after fracture.

records.question: A man presents with a slowly progressive swelling over the past 1 and 1/2 years. On examination, it has a variable consistency and appears as shown in the image. What is the probable cause?
records.explanation: A slow-growing mixed-consistency salivary mass can suggest pleomorphic adenoma. Location, imaging and tissue assessment are needed to distinguish other salivary tumours.

records.question: Painful arc syndrome is seen in all except:
records.explanation: A painful arc often reflects subacromial impingement. A complete supraspinatus tear can instead cause marked weakness, but pain patterns alone cannot definitively exclude a tear.

records.question: What is shown in the given image?
records.explanation: A skin cyst with a punctum and keratinous contents often represents an epidermoid cyst, commonly miscalled sebaceous cyst. The photograph must establish its characteristics.

records.question: De-gloving injury refers to_____?
options: Skin and subcutaneous fat are stripped from the underlying fascia
Skin, subcutaneous fat and fascia are stripped from tendons
Skin, subcutaneous fat, fascia and tendons are stripped from bone
records.explanation: Shearing separates skin and subcutaneous tissue from deeper fascia, disrupting perforating vessels. The injury may be open or concealed beneath intact skin.

records.question: Rheumatoid arthritis management in a patient with deformity is?
records.explanation: A biologic such as an anti-TNF agent may be added after inadequate response to appropriate conventional therapy. Existing deformity alone does not determine drug choice or replace infection screening.

records.question: A female patient presents with a breast abscess. Under antibiotic cover, an aspiration was attempted which failed to reveal any aspirate. What is the next step in management?
options: Stop antibiotics as no aspirate was collected
records.explanation: An unsuccessful aspiration requires reassessment of localisation, contents and technique, often with ultrasound. Repeat image-guided aspiration may help, but persistent or complex collections may need other drainage.

records.question: A 60 year old woman presents with low backache and on a lumbar CT the following is seen. What is your diagnosis?
records.explanation: Reduced bone strength can cause vertebral compression fractures. CT morphology and clinical assessment are needed; osteoporosis diagnosis is not established solely by an unspecified scan image.

records.question: Which nerve is involved in Frey's syndrome?
records.explanation: Aberrant regeneration of auriculotemporal parasympathetic fibres toward cutaneous sweat glands produces gustatory sweating after parotid-region injury.

records.question: An 18-year-old boy presents to the orthopedician with complaints of painful swelling below the knee joint. An X-Ray was obtained which is given below. Which of the following is the preferred treatment modality for this patient?
records.explanation: Extended curettage and grafting can treat selected benign aggressive bone lesions. The image and tissue diagnosis must establish the lesion before endorsing this operation.

records.question: The following images A and B show?
records.explanation: Jersey finger avulses flexor digitorum profundus; mallet or baseball finger injures terminal extensor function. The individual images must be matched to the respective loss of movement.

records.question: Which of the following statements is false regarding deep vein thrombosis (DVT)?
options: Most common clinical presentation is pain and tenderness in calf
Some cases may directly present as pulmonary thromboembolism
records.explanation: Leg DVT commonly presents unilaterally. Bilateral thrombosis can occur, but describing most DVT as bilateral is incorrect.

records.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding the dose-response curve shown in the image below?
options: C is more potent than A
B is more potent than A
records.explanation: A reversible competitive antagonist typically shifts an agonist curve rightward without reducing its achievable maximum. The plotted axes and responses are required to identify curve B.

records.question: A truck driver presents with dilated, tortuous veins of 4 mm in the foot. What is the stage of clinical classification according to CEAP (ClinicaI-etioIogy-anatomy-pathophysiology for chronic venous disorders)?
records.explanation: CEAP clinical class C2 denotes varicose veins, generally at least three millimetres when measured upright. Oedema and skin changes belong to higher classes.

records.question: Which of the following antiglaucoma medications is unsafe in infants?
records.explanation: Brimonidine can cause serious central nervous system and respiratory depression in infants and young children. Its use is restricted by age-specific contraindications and warnings.

records.question: Apparent volume of distribution of a drug is very high (6L/kg). Which of the following is true regarding the distribution of that drug?
records.explanation: An apparent distribution volume much larger than body water suggests extensive tissue binding or sequestration relative to plasma concentration. It is not a literal anatomical fluid volume.

records.question: Which of the following phases of a clinical trial is also referred to as an efficacy trial?
records.explanation: Phase II trials explore efficacy and dose in affected patients while continuing safety assessment. Phase III also assesses efficacy in larger confirmatory studies, so the label is not exclusive.

records.question: Which of the following is not a part of revised trauma score (RTS)?
records.explanation: The Revised Trauma Score uses Glasgow Coma Scale, systolic pressure and respiratory rate. Pulse rate is not one of its scored components.

records.question: Which of the following is an oral factor Xa inhibitor?
records.explanation: Rivaroxaban is an oral direct factor Xa inhibitor that reduces thrombin generation. It differs from indirect heparin-mediated inhibition and vitamin-K antagonism.

records.question: What is the drug of choice for diphtheria carrier state?
records.explanation: A macrolide such as erythromycin is a recognised option for eradication in diphtheria carriers. Current public-health guidance, resistance and post-treatment cultures determine management.

records.question: What is the mechanism of action of oseltamivir and zanamivir?
records.explanation: Oseltamivir and zanamivir inhibit viral neuraminidase, reducing release of new influenza particles from infected cells. They do not directly block viral protein synthesis.

records.question: Which of the following is a synthetic PFG2 alpha derivative used as an abortifacient?
records.explanation: Carboprost is a prostaglandin F2-alpha analogue that stimulates uterine contraction. Its indication, route and contraindications must be distinguished from those of other prostaglandins.

records.question: Which of the following drugs causes activation of K+-ATP channels?
records.explanation: Nicorandil opens ATP-sensitive potassium channels and has nitrate-like effects, promoting vascular relaxation. Its mechanism differs from a pure calcium-channel blocker.

records.question: Most effective antiemetic for chemotherapy – induced vomiting is _____________.
records.explanation: Granisetron blocks 5-HT3 receptors and helps prevent chemotherapy-induced emesis. Best prophylaxis depends on emetic risk and often combines several drug classes.

records.question: Nasal polyps are commonly associated with: -
records.explanation: Nasal polyps commonly associate with asthma and aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease. The older intrinsic-asthma label is imprecise and does not cover every mechanism.

records.question: True statement about teduglutide is:
options: It is recommended for patients with colorectal cancer
records.explanation: Teduglutide is a GLP-2 analogue that promotes intestinal adaptation and absorption. It is used for selected short-bowel-syndrome patients requiring parenteral support.

records.question: Cisatracurium is preferred over atracurium because?
options: It has rapid onset of action
It has less depressant action on heart
It has short duration of action
It causes less release of histamine
records.explanation: Cisatracurium generally releases less histamine than atracurium at clinical doses, reducing associated haemodynamic effects. Both require appropriate neuromuscular monitoring.

records.question: All of the following are AIDS defining illnesses except:
records.explanation: Oesophageal candidiasis is an AIDS-defining illness, whereas uncomplicated oral candidiasis alone is not. Both can indicate clinically important immune dysfunction.

records.question: A 47 year old man with a diagnosis of acute myeloid leukemia with a blood type O negative blood group presents to the transplant clinic to discuss proceeding with an allogeneic stem cell transplant. Which of the following would be an optimal donor?
options: His HHLA identical 50-year-old brother who is otherwise healthy and is blood type O+
An HLA identical matched unrelated donor who is blood type
records.explanation: An HLA-matched healthy sibling is often a strong allogeneic donor candidate. ABO or Rh mismatch does not automatically exclude donation, and broader donor factors still matter.

records.question: Which of the following fluoroquinolones has maximum bioavailability?
records.explanation: Levofloxacin has near-complete oral bioavailability. Several other fluoroquinolones also have high values, so maximum requires checking the listed agents and formulation.

records.question: A dermatologist wants to prescribe acitretin to a patient with psoriasis. Which of the following statements is false regarding the drug?
options: It can cause increased sensitivity to sunlight
Female patients should avoid getting pregnant for 6 months after therapy
Acitretin has a half life of about 50 hours
records.explanation: Acitretin is highly teratogenic and pregnancy must be avoided for the required prolonged period after treatment, commonly three years. Six months is insufficient under standard labelling.

records.question: A 30-year-old HIV positive man presents with fever for 3 weeks, dry cough an significant weight loss. His chest x-ray is given below. What is the most likely diagnosis?
records.explanation: Advanced HIV with subacute dry cough and respiratory symptoms raises concern for Pneumocystis pneumonia. Imaging and organism-directed testing are needed to distinguish other causes.

records.question: Cilastatin is administered to prolong the action of which of the following drugs?
records.explanation: Cilastatin inhibits renal dehydropeptidase I, reducing imipenem degradation and improving active drug exposure. It is not an antibacterial substitute itself.

records.question: What is the drug used to differentiate myasthenia gravis from cholinergic crisis?
records.explanation: Edrophonium was historically used in assessing myasthenic weakness, but can cause serious cholinergic effects. It is not a routine safe bedside shortcut for differentiating acute crises.

records.question: All are true about Guillain-Barre syndrome except:
records.explanation: Classic GBS often progresses from leg weakness upward with reduced reflexes. Variants exist, but a descending pattern is not the usual teaching description and requires alternative diagnoses to be considered.

records.question: Which of the following is true about pegylated – filgrastim?
options: Duration of action is shorter than normal filgrastim
Added advantage is that it can be taken orally
It should not be administered in sickle cell patients
It is not effective in the treatment of severe neutropenia
records.explanation: G-CSF products carry warnings about severe sickle-cell crises in affected patients. A blanket rule should be checked against current labelling and specialist risk assessment rather than assumed from this recall.

records.question: Which of the following is the best treatment for idiopathic thrombocytic purpura?
records.explanation: Splenectomy can provide durable response in selected persistent ITP. It is not universally the best initial treatment; bleeding risk, disease duration and medical options guide care.

records.question: The best approach in the treatment of chronic SIADH is _____________
options: Reducing fluid intake to <500 ml per day
records.explanation: Tolvaptan can increase free-water excretion in selected SIADH cases, but is not universal first-line treatment. Cause treatment, fluid measures and controlled sodium correction are essential.

records.question: Which cardiac chamber enlargement is seen in the case of mitral stenosis on chest x-ray initially?
records.explanation: Mitral obstruction raises left-atrial pressure and can enlarge the left atrium. Pulmonary vascular and right-heart changes may develop subsequently.

records.question: Intravenous mannitol is used in ____________?
records.explanation: Intravenous mannitol can acutely lower markedly raised intraocular pressure through an osmotic effect. It is not routine chronic therapy for every glaucoma patient.

records.question: Which of the following carbapenems has increased risk of causing seizures?
records.explanation: Imipenem can provoke seizures, particularly with high exposure, renal impairment or central nervous system disease. Dose adjustment and patient-specific risk matter.

records.question: Which among the following is false?
options: Components of MELD (model for end stage liver disease) scoring system are creatinine, bilirubin, international normalized ratio (INR), serum sodium (mEq/L)
Components of CTP (child Turcotte Pugh) score are albumin, bilirubin, INR, ascites encephalopathy
Components of CTP (child Turcotte Pugh) are creatinine, bilirubin, international normalized ratio (INR)
MELD score is used to assess and prioritize patients awaiting liver transplantation
records.explanation: Child-Pugh scoring uses bilirubin, albumin, coagulation, ascites and encephalopathy. Creatinine belongs to other liver-risk models rather than the standard Child-Pugh variables.

records.question: Which of the following helps in maintaining the patency of ductus arteriosus?
records.explanation: Prostaglandin E1 can maintain ductus arteriosus patency in selected duct-dependent congenital heart disease. Administration requires monitored specialist care.

records.question: Identify the false statement about the bundle of Kent
options: It is faster than AV nodal pathway
It is slower than AV nodal pathway
records.explanation: An accessory atrioventricular pathway can conduct outside normal AV-nodal delay and produce ventricular pre-excitation. Calling it necessarily slower than the AV node is false.

records.question: Osborn waves in ECG are seen in:
records.explanation: Hypothermia can produce prominent J or Osborn waves at the QRS-ST junction. Other causes exist, so the ECG finding requires temperature and clinical correlation.

records.question: The production of which of the following hormones is increased in obesity?
records.explanation: Insulin resistance in obesity often produces compensatory hyperinsulinaemia. Levels depend on beta-cell function and diabetes stage, so increased insulin is not universal.

records.question: What is the diagnosis of this patient from the ECG shown below?
records.explanation: A ventricular-origin tachyarrhythmia commonly has wide QRS complexes. The tracing is needed to confirm VT and distinguish other wide-complex rhythms.

records.question: Which of the following parameters would you use to check the efficiency of the surveillance system for malaria under the National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme?
records.explanation: Annual Blood Examination Rate measures the proportion of a population tested for malaria over a year. It reflects surveillance activity rather than test sensitivity or disease incidence alone.

records.question: All are true about patients with trigeminal neuralgia except:
options: Pain along V2 and V3 division of trigeminal nerve
No objective signs of sensory loss
records.explanation: Classical trigeminal neuralgia causes brief electric-shock-like attacks in a trigeminal distribution, often with tactile triggers. Deep continuous pain is less typical and warrants broader assessment.

records.question: Which of the following is false regarding confounding factors?
options: It can be reduced by matching
It is associated individually with both cause and effect
It is distributed equally in both study and control groups
It is associated with the exposure of the study
records.explanation: A confounder must relate to exposure and outcome without being an intermediate. Equal distribution between groups generally reduces confounding from that factor rather than defining it.

records.question: Which of the following is the best level of prevention of breast cancer?
records.explanation: Early diagnosis and prompt treatment are secondary-prevention measures. Whether a screening strategy is best depends on evidence, population and the distinction from primary risk reduction.

records.question: What is the dosage of vitamin A given for a 2-year-old baby with keratomalacia?
options: 2,00,000 IU immediately, followed by same dose after 24 hours
1,00,000 IU immediately, followed by the same dose after 1 week
1,00,000 IU immediately, followed by the same dose after 24 hours and after a week
2,00,000 IU immediately, followed by the same dose 24 hours later and after 2 weeks
records.explanation: Clinical xerophthalmia in a child older than twelve months uses age-specific high-dose vitamin A with repeat dosing under recognised protocols. Confirm diagnosis, timing and prior doses rather than applying the schedule indiscriminately.

records.question: In a normal curve, what is the percentage of distribution of one standard deviation?
records.explanation: Approximately 68.3 percent of values in a normal distribution lie between one standard deviation below and above the mean.

records.question: According to IMNCI, a 6-month-old child is said to have pneumonia if the child has fast breathing with a respiratory rate more than:
records.explanation: For ages two to below twelve months, the IMCI fast-breathing threshold is fifty or more breaths per minute. More than fifty would wrongly exclude a rate of exactly fifty.

records.question: Which of the following is part of the concurrent list of the Indian Constitution?
options: Fishing and fisheries beyond territorial waters
records.explanation: Adulteration of foodstuffs and other goods appears in the Constitution's Concurrent List. This concerns legislative competence, not the complete operational food-safety law.

records.question: All of the following are features of Crohn’s disease except:
records.explanation: Loss of colonic haustration producing a lead-pipe appearance is classically associated with chronic ulcerative colitis, rather than the typical skip-lesion Crohn pattern.

records.question: Which of the following is the most common type of Guillain-Barre syndrome?
records.explanation: Acute inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy is common in many Western cohorts. Axonal variants are more frequent in some regions, so most common depends on geography and population.

records.question: Cushing’s ulcers are seen in
records.explanation: Cushing ulcers are stress-related gastroduodenal ulcers associated with intracranial disease or injury. They differ from Curling ulcers classically associated with severe burns.

records.question: Which of the following is true about paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria?
records.explanation: PNH clones lack GPI-anchored proteins including CD55 and CD59, making blood cells vulnerable to complement injury. Flow cytometry assesses this deficiency.

records.question: A patient with rheumatoid arthritis has been treated with methotrexate and low-dose corticosteroids for the past 4 months. However, the disease is still progressing. What would be your recommendation for the further management of this patient?
options: Stop oral methotrexate and start parenteral methotrexate
records.explanation: Adding sulfasalazine and hydroxychloroquine creates conventional triple therapy with methotrexate. Treatment escalation depends on disease activity, prior optimisation, prognostic factors and biologic alternatives.

records.question: A lady presents with fever, oral ulcer, photosensitivity, and rashes on her face as shown below. What is the most likely diagnosis?
records.explanation: Photosensitivity, oral ulcers and systemic symptoms can support SLE, but rash appearance and immunological assessment are needed. These findings alone do not establish every classification criterion.

records.question: Which of the following murmur increases on standing?
records.explanation: Standing reduces ventricular filling and can increase dynamic left-ventricular outflow obstruction in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, intensifying its murmur. Mitral-prolapse findings can also change.

records.question: On performing a pulmonary function test, reduction in FEV1/FVC is characteristic of:
records.explanation: A reduced FEV1/FVC ratio suggests airflow obstruction. Interpretation uses suitable reference limits and clinical context, with bronchodilator testing when indicated.

records.question: Calcitonin levels are increased in:
records.explanation: Calcitonin responds to calcium and is a marker of medullary thyroid disease. Hyperparathyroid hypercalcaemia can influence secretion, but it is not a specific diagnostic association without the alternatives and context.

records.question: A 4-year-old male child developed sore throat and difficulty in swallowing and mild fever. On examination, the clinical picture shown below is seen. Which of the following sentences is false regarding the vaccine that could have prevented this condition?
options: Its administered on the anterolateral aspect of thigh
A prior adverse reaction with temperature above 37 degrees is a contraindication
Cellular pertussis component in the vaccine is not recommended after 7-years of age
The diphtheria toxoid dose in adults is much lesser than the pediatric dose
records.explanation: A minor illness or low-grade fever is not usually a vaccination contraindication. True contraindications depend on the vaccine and reaction, such as a severe allergic response.

records.question: The principal unit of administration in India is____?
records.explanation: The district is conventionally described as a principal unit of Indian field administration. Responsibilities and service structures depend on the state and administrative programme.

records.question: Cross product ratio can be arrived from:
records.explanation: The cross-product ratio from a two-by-two case-control table estimates an odds ratio. It is not automatically the same as relative risk.

records.question: In controlled tipping, the amount of land required for the trench method to be practiced for a population of 10,000 is:
records.explanation: Older public-health texts quote approximate trench-landfill land requirements. Actual design depends on waste generation, soil, depth, compaction, cover and environmental regulation rather than population alone.

records.question: The test of choice to measure the difference in means between two groups in a study, with one group being a control is:
records.explanation: An unpaired t-test compares means from independent groups when its assumptions are suitable. Unequal variance, nonnormality, paired data or more groups may require a different method.

records.question: The test of significance done for two or more proportions?
records.explanation: A chi-square test can compare categorical proportions when expected counts and independence assumptions are appropriate. Small counts may require an exact method.

records.question: If a patient tests positive for a disease, which of the following represents the probability of her actually having the disease?
records.explanation: Positive predictive value is the proportion of positive test results that truly have disease. It depends on disease prevalence as well as test performance.

records.question: In the following natural history of disease flowchart, point A to C is called as?
records.explanation: Lead time is the interval by which screening advances diagnosis before usual clinical detection. The labelled timeline is needed to verify that points A and C mark those events.

records.question: The following diagram charts the population change over years from 1983 to 1989 in a given place. What is the statistical diagram used here?
records.explanation: A component or stacked bar divides each bar into constituent categories while displaying totals. The actual graph must be checked before distinguishing it from grouped bars or a line plot.

records.question: Triage is done during disaster management to ensure treatment of casualties is done properly. What is true about triage done at the disaster site?
options: Green labels are for those who need to be transported on priority
Moribund patients receive the lowest priority
Most commonly used system is three color code system
records.explanation: Under severe resource constraints, expectant casualties may receive lower immediate intervention priority than salvageable critically injured patients. Triage is dynamic, and comfort care remains necessary.

records.question: The risk of genetic diseases in consanguineous marriage between first cousins is?
records.explanation: First-cousin parentage increases the chance of shared recessive variants. Absolute risk depends on background population, family history and the outcome defined; one percentage cannot describe every genetic disease.

records.question: A paradoxical carrier is defined as:
options: A person who sheds pathogens during incubation period
A carrier who acquired pathogen from another carrier
A person who acquired pathogen from patient
A patient who became a carrier
records.explanation: Paradoxical carrier is a traditional epidemiological term for a carrier infected by another carrier. Modern investigation focuses on the actual transmission chain and infectious state.

records.question: Which of the following vaccine is contraindicated in pregnancy?
records.explanation: Live attenuated varicella vaccine is contraindicated during pregnancy. Post-exposure assessment and postpartum vaccination follow separate guidance; inadvertent vaccination does not itself mandate termination.

records.question: What is the best way to plot the changes in incidence of a disease in a given area over time?
records.explanation: A line graph displays values in chronological order and makes incidence trends easier to see. Rates must use consistent denominators and reporting intervals.

records.question: Which of the following is false about Rubella infection?
options: It is a type of droplet infection
Infection in early pregnancy causes a milder form of disease in the fetus
Fetus affected in late pregnancy may have only deafness
records.explanation: Maternal rubella early in pregnancy carries greater risk of severe congenital effects. Saying early infection produces milder fetal disease reverses the usual risk pattern.

records.question: A resident doctor sustained a needlestick injury while sampling blood of a patient who is HIV positive. A decision is taken to offer him post-exposure prophylaxis. Which one of the following would be the best recommendation?
records.explanation: An appropriate three-drug regimen, commonly tenofovir, lamivudine and dolutegravir, is used for twenty-eight days after qualifying exposure under current guidance. Start promptly after assessment rather than waiting for symptoms.

records.question: Calculate the therapeutic index of a drug whose dose-response curves are plotted as shown below:
records.explanation: Therapeutic index conventionally divides a median toxic or lethal dose by the median effective dose. The plotted numerical values are needed to verify a ratio of four.

records.question: Which nerve passes through the foramen marked in the image below?
records.explanation: The inferior alveolar nerve enters the mandibular foramen and travels within the mandibular canal. The labelled foramen must be identified before confirming this answer.

records.question: A 40 year old male patient came to ED with complaints of weakness, paresthesia, and breathing difficulty. Relevant investigations were done. The ECG obtained is suggestive of:
records.explanation: Hypokalaemia can cause flattened T waves, ST depression and prominent U waves. The ECG and serum potassium are needed to establish the abnormality and urgency.

records.question: All the following statement are true about Frey’s Syndrome except:
options: Aberrant misdirection of parasympathetic fibers of auriculotemporal nerve
Botulinum toxin is one of the treatment suggested
Less chances with enucleation than paratidectomy
records.explanation: Frey syndrome reflects aberrant nerve regeneration after parotid-region injury. Comparisons between enucleation and parotidectomy depend on technique and outcome ascertainment; operative choice is not based on this complication alone.

records.question: A 60 year old patient presented with Hoarseness of voice. On examination following finding shown below. What could be the diagnosis?
records.explanation: Hoarseness may reflect laryngeal pathology or recurrent-laryngeal nerve dysfunction from several causes. The pictured findings and examination are required before calling a neck mass metastatic.

records.question: A 65 year old female patient is brought to the emergency department in a state of unconsciousness. Her BP is 70/50 mm of Hg. Her ECG is shown below. What is the next best step in the management of her condition?
records.explanation: A haemodynamically unstable organised tachyarrhythmia with a pulse may require synchronised cardioversion. Pulseless or polymorphic rhythms instead require the appropriate defibrillation pathway; the ECG and pulse are essential.

records.question: A 56-year-old male presents to the physician with complaints of progressive bilateral prominence and bulging of eyes for 1 month. He is a known case of Grave's disease. He is other otherwise vitally stable, and other general physical examination reveals a swelling in front of the neck, which moves upwards on swallowing but doesn't move on protruding tongue. The image of the patient's eyes is shown in the image below. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis of the patient's current symptoms?
records.explanation: Graves-associated orbitopathy can cause bilateral proptosis through orbital inflammation and tissue expansion. Vision-threatening signs require urgent assessment; other proptosis causes should be excluded.

records.question: What is the name of this triangle?
records.explanation: The gastrinoma triangle is a defined anatomical region containing many sporadic gastrinomas. Its boundaries must be matched to the displayed diagram before naming the marked triangle.

records.question: Which of the following forms the lateral boundary of the anatomical snuff box?
options: Extensor pollicis brevis and abductor pollicis longus
Extensor pollicis longus and abductor pollicis brevis
Extensor pollicis longus and extensor pollicis brevis
Abductor pollicis longus and abductor pollicis brevis
records.explanation: Abductor pollicis longus and extensor pollicis brevis form the lateral snuffbox border; extensor pollicis longus forms its medial border.

records.question: The remnants of Wolffian ducts in females are located in
records.explanation: Mesonephric remnants such as the epoophoron and paroophoron persist near the ovary within the broad ligament. Gartner remnants may extend into the vaginal wall.

records.question: Which of the following is not used for the identification of the facial nerve trunk?
records.explanation: Facial-nerve identification uses landmarks near the parotid and mastoid, including the posterior digastric belly. Inferior omohyoid lies outside this operative region.

records.question: In which part of the fallopian tube does fertilization occur?
records.explanation: Fertilisation normally occurs in the tubal ampulla, where the oocyte encounters sperm before the conceptus travels toward the uterine cavity.

records.question: The false statement about fetal circulation is:
options: Anatomical closure of foramen ovale is by 3 to 5 days
Anatomical closure of ductus venosus is by 3 to 7 days
Anatomical closure of ductus arteriosus is by 2 to 3 weeks
records.explanation: Postnatal pressure changes promote functional closure, but anatomical fusion takes substantially longer and may remain incomplete. Three-to-five-day anatomical closure is therefore inaccurate.

records.question: A patient presented with clinical features of ataxia and incoordination. This is due to thrombosis of which artery?
records.explanation: Superior cerebellar artery infarction can cause ataxia and incoordination.

records.question: A patient came to the gynaecology OPD with complaints of foul – smelling frothy vaginal discharge and intense itching. On examination, the cervix was spotted and had the appearance of a strawberry. Identify the causative organism.
records.explanation: Trichomonas can produce irritating frothy discharge and punctate cervical erythema. Examination findings support testing rather than proving the organism without confirmation.

records.question: Which of the following structures prevents the upward extension of thyroid swelling through its attachment to the thyroid cartilage?
records.explanation: Sternothyroid attachment to the thyroid cartilage limits upward expansion of a thyroid swelling. Fascial attachments separately explain movement with swallowing.

records.question: Identify the contraceptive shown in the given image
records.explanation: An internal condom lines the vagina as a barrier method. The device photograph is required to distinguish it from a diaphragm or another contraceptive.

records.question: A patient presented with the extension of MCP joint and flexion of IP joints. Which muscle is affected?
records.explanation: Lumbricals and interossei flex MCP joints and extend IP joints. Their weakness permits the opposite clawing posture through unopposed extrinsic muscle actions.

records.question: A woman presents to the OPD with complaints of amenorrhoea for the past year. She has a history of postpartum hemorrhage and lactational failure. What is the probable diagnosis ?
records.explanation: Severe obstetric haemorrhage can infarct the enlarged pituitary, causing postpartum lactation failure and subsequent amenorrhoea from anterior pituitary hormone deficiencies.

records.question: What is the function of the proteasome?
records.explanation: Proteasomes degrade selected intracellular proteins, often after ubiquitin tagging, supporting protein quality control and regulated protein turnover.

records.question: Meiosis occurs in:
records.explanation: Oocytes resume meiosis during reproductive cycles, but completion of meiosis II ordinarily follows fertilisation. The statement depends on the meiotic stage intended.

records.question: An 18 year old girl presents with a history of low – grade fever, weight loss, abdominal pain and amenorrhoea for six months. On examination, a pelvic mass is felt on the left side and signs of ascites are positive. What is your diagnosis ?
records.explanation: Genital tuberculosis can cause amenorrhoea, adnexal masses and ascites. These nonspecific findings also require evaluation for other infection and malignancy.

records.question: Replacing alanine by which amino acid, will increase the UV absorbance of protein at 280nm wavelength?
records.explanation: Tryptophan's aromatic side chain strongly absorbs near 280 nm. Replacing nonaromatic alanine with tryptophan therefore increases protein absorbance at that wavelength.

records.question: The long left recurrent laryngeal nerve is due to the persistence of which arch artery?
records.explanation: Persistence of the left sixth-arch ductal connection retains the left recurrent laryngeal nerve beneath the aortic-ductal region, creating its longer thoracic course.

records.question: A patient presented with weakness of the right side of the face with the loss of pain and temperature. Pain and temperature sensation of the left leg is also lost. The lesion is most likely located at?
records.explanation: Ipsilateral facial involvement with contralateral body pain-temperature loss suggests lateral pontine injury. Full examination is needed to define the vascular territory and affected pathways.

records.question: Ligation of common hepatic artery will impair blood supply in:
options: Right gastric and right gastroepiploic artery
Right gastric and left gastric artery
Right gastroepiploic and short gastric vessels
Right gastric and short gastric vessels
records.explanation: The right gastric and gastroduodenal-derived right gastroepiploic supplies depend on hepatic arterial anatomy. Ligation level and collateral flow affect the actual perfusion consequences.

records.question: Vitamin B12 is found maximum in:
records.explanation: Animal-derived foods are major natural B12 sources. Fortified foods also provide B12; unfortified plant foods are not reliable sources.

records.question: Identify the sign shown in the image below:
records.explanation: Biceps tendon rupture can allow muscle-belly retraction and a Popeye contour.

records.question: The process of apolipoprotein B48 synthesis involves which of the following?
records.explanation: Intestinal RNA editing introduces a premature stop in the ApoB transcript, producing shorter ApoB48 instead of hepatic ApoB100.

records.question: A patient presents with a clinical scenario of obstructive jaundice. Which of the following results can be seen in Van der Bergh’s reaction?
records.explanation: Conjugated bilirubin reacts directly in the diazo assay, explaining a direct-positive reaction in many obstructive jaundice presentations.

records.question: A patient presented with an enlarged inguinal lymph node. The most likely primary cause is
records.explanation: The anal canal below the pectinate line drains to superficial inguinal nodes. Inguinal enlargement has many other causes, so location alone does not establish anal cancer.

records.question: In modern obstetrics, which of the following investigations is used for monitoring the fetus of an Rh- negative sensitized mother ?
records.explanation: Anaemia raises fetal middle-cerebral-artery peak systolic velocity through altered viscosity and haemodynamics. Interpretation uses gestation-adjusted values and specialist surveillance.

records.question: What is the causative agent for granuloma inguinale ?
records.explanation: Granuloma inguinale is caused by Klebsiella granulomatis, historically called Calymmatobacterium granulomatis.

records.question: Which of the following is the causative organism of vulval warts?
records.explanation: Low-risk HPV types, especially 6 and 11, commonly cause anogenital warts. Their appearance does not identify an oncogenic HPV type.

records.question: A tumor of the uncinate process of the pancreas affects which of the following vessels?
records.explanation: The pancreatic uncinate process lies close to the superior mesenteric vessels. Tumour involvement of this relationship is important for staging and resectability.

records.question: If the percentage of thymine residues in DNA is 28%. What is the % of cytosine?
records.explanation: In double-stranded DNA, thymine equals adenine. If each is twenty-eight percent, the remaining forty-four percent splits equally into guanine and cytosine, giving twenty-two percent cytosine.

records.question: A 22 year old pregnant woman at 13 weeks of gestation informs you about accidental exposure to radiation from a chest X – ray at 7 weeks of gestation. What should be the next advised to her ?
records.explanation: A routine maternal chest radiograph gives a very low fetal dose and ordinarily does not justify termination. Confirm the actual exposure and provide dose-based counselling.

records.question: Enzyme activated by a decrease in insulin: glucagon ration is:
records.explanation: A lower insulin-to-glucagon ratio promotes hepatic glucose production, including glucose-6-phosphatase expression and activity in the gluconeogenic programme.

records.question: Which of the following is true regarding non-competitive inhibition?
records.explanation: A pure noncompetitive inhibitor reduces available catalytic capacity and Vmax without changing Km. Mixed inhibition need not preserve Km.

records.question: From which of the following structure does the saccule develop?
records.explanation: The inferior part of the otic vesicle contributes the saccule and cochlear duct. The superior division contributes utricular and semicircular structures.

records.question: After successful delivery of the baby, the obstetrician witnesses that the episiotomy performed has extended backwards beyond the perineal body. Which among the following structures is likely to be injured in this case?
records.explanation: A tear extending through the anal-sphincter complex involves the external sphincter. Exact grading requires checking internal sphincter and anorectal mucosal involvement too.

records.question: What is the surgery done to widen the cartilaginous part of the external auditory canal called?
records.explanation: Meatoplasty widens the external auditory meatus, especially its cartilaginous opening. It differs from procedures directed primarily at the bony canal.

records.question: Cough on scratching the external acoustic canal is due to?
records.explanation: Auricular vagal sensory stimulation in the ear canal can trigger coughing. This is the ear-cough or Arnold reflex.

records.question: A patient came to the hospital with a complaint of abdominal pain. Routine investigations were unremarkable. On observation, the urine turned black on standing. Which of the following enzymes is likely to be defective in this patient?
records.explanation: Homogentisate dioxygenase deficiency permits homogentisic acid accumulation. Oxidation on standing darkens urine and chronic tissue deposition can cause ochronosis.

records.question: A 34-year-old male as on maize as a staple diet for a prolonged period. He presented with diarrhea and a lesion over his neck as shown in the image below. The condition occurs due to deficiency of:
records.explanation: Niacin deficiency can cause photosensitive dermatitis, diarrhoea and neurological dysfunction. Maize-dominant diets are a risk; the pictured rash still requires confirmation.

records.question: A person who met with an accident, and suffered from a skull fracture presents with the following finding. Identify this clinical finding.
records.explanation: Postauricular bruising can indicate a basilar skull fracture. The photograph and trauma assessment are needed; the sign may be delayed.

records.question: Which vitamin, when infused in supraphysiological doses, causes macular edema and macular cysts?
records.explanation: High-dose nicotinic acid can cause cystoid macular changes. This pharmacological adverse effect should not be confused with ordinary dietary niacin intake.

records.question: A 16 year old girl presents to the OPD with a history of primary amenorrhoea and cyclical pain. Perineal examination reveals a bulge protruding from the vagina. Identify the cause of this presentation.
options: Transverse septum in the proximal vagina
records.explanation: An imperforate hymen can obstruct menstrual outflow, causing primary amenorrhoea, cyclical pain and a bulging hymenal membrane from retained blood.

records.question: Surgery where one nostril is partially or completely occluded is done for which condition?
records.explanation: Temporary nostril closure in Young-type procedures reduces airflow and drying in selected severe atrophic rhinitis. It is not routine treatment for every case.

records.question: Nitric oxide is synthesized from
records.explanation: Nitric-oxide synthase converts arginine into nitric oxide and citrulline using oxygen and reducing cofactors. Nitric oxide then activates soluble guanylate cyclase.

records.question: What is occipitomental view with open mouth also known as?
records.explanation: Waters view is an occipitomental projection commonly used for maxillary sinus assessment. An open-mouth variation improves visualisation of additional structures.

records.question: A 9-year-old boy comes with complaints of right ear pain, difficulty in opening the mouth, painful swallowing, and fever. The oral cavity examination reveals the following. The external facial examination is unremarkable. Which of the following is likely?
records.explanation: Peritonsillar abscess can cause severe throat pain, trismus, referred otalgia and asymmetrical oropharyngeal swelling.

records.question: A pregnant woman presents for a routine antenatal checkup at 18 weeks of gestation. On abdominal examination, the uterine size was found to correspond to 16 weeks of gestation. On USG, oligohydramnios was found. Which of the following is a likely cause ?
records.explanation: Bilateral renal agenesis markedly reduces fetal urine and can cause severe oligohydramnios. Other renal, membrane and placental causes require assessment.

records.question: A 24 year old woman visits the infertility clinic with a complaint of recurrent abortions. Upon investigations, she is found to have a septate uterus. Which of the following corrective procedures has the best obstetric outcome ?
records.explanation: Hysteroscopic septum incision may be considered in selected patients after counselling. Evidence, reproductive history and correct anomaly classification determine benefit; surgery is not universally required.

records.question: Which of the following layers is responsible for maintaining the hydration and transparency of the cornea?
records.explanation: Corneal endothelium maintains stromal deturgescence through barrier and pump functions. Endothelial failure allows oedema and loss of transparency.

records.question: What is the characteristic feature of a fungal ulcer?
options: Dendritic ulcer on a fluorescein dye
records.explanation: Feathery borders and satellite infiltrates can support fungal keratitis. These are suggestive features rather than proof, so microscopy and culture guide diagnosis.

records.question: Extra row of eyelashes behind the grey line is called as?
records.explanation: Distichiasis is an additional row of lashes emerging near meibomian-gland openings. It differs from trichiasis, where normal lashes are misdirected.

records.question: A middle-aged woman presented with bilateral proptosis, restriction of eye movements, and chemosis. Her thyroid profile showed she was euthyroid. What is the most probable cause?
records.explanation: Thyroid eye disease can occur despite normal current thyroid hormone levels. Clinical and orbital assessment must exclude other causes of bilateral proptosis.

records.question: The drug increasing uveoscleral flow is?
records.explanation: Latanoprost is a prostaglandin analogue that increases aqueous outflow, particularly through the uveoscleral pathway, lowering intraocular pressure.

records.question: A 33 year old female patient comes with complaints of menorrhagia for the past 3 months. The duration and regularity of her menstrual cycles are normal. Non – hormonal management has been tried without success. What is the most appropriate next step?
records.explanation: Hormonal therapy can reduce bleeding after suitable assessment, but choice depends on cause, fertility plans and contraindications rather than failure of any single nonhormonal option.

records.question: Photostress test is used to differentiate between:
records.explanation: Delayed visual recovery after photostress supports macular dysfunction more than isolated optic-nerve disease. The test supplements examination rather than replacing retinal assessment.

records.question: Shifting fluid sign is seen in?
records.explanation: Subretinal fluid can shift with position in an exudative retinal detachment. The underlying inflammatory, vascular or tumour-related cause requires examination.

records.question: A 35 year old primigravida who conceived after in vitro fertilization therapy came for an antenatal checkup at 38 weeks of gestation. Her obstetric history revealed that she was pregnant with DCDA twins. On examination, the first twin was found to be in a breech position and the maternal blood pressure was found to be greater than 140/90 mm Hg on two occasions with grade 1+ proteinuria. What should be done next?
options: Monitor BP and terminate pregnancy if BP rises
Terminate pregnancy at 40 weeks of gestation
records.explanation: A non-cephalic first twin commonly favours planned caesarean delivery. Immediate emergency delivery is not implied solely by presentation in an otherwise stable antenatal assessment.

records.question: Which of the following is the correct statement regarding Huntington’s chorea?
options: It is a trinucleotide repeat disorder
There is a loss of function type of mutation
There are abnormal repeats of CUG
Abnormality is seen due to mutation in chromosome 6
records.explanation: Huntington disease involves a CAG repeat expansion in HTT, with autosomal-dominant inheritance and possible anticipation. Repeat size affects risk and expected onset.

records.question: Which of the following statements is true about the pathology of achalasia cardia?
options: Decreased release of No and VIP in the distal part of esophagus
Decreased tone of the lower esophageal sphincter
records.explanation: Loss of inhibitory myenteric signalling, including nitric oxide and VIP pathways, impairs lower-oesophageal-sphincter relaxation in achalasia.

records.question: Which of the following effects of puberty are not mediated by estrogen ?
records.explanation: Pubic and axillary hair development is principally androgen-dependent. Oestrogen primarily drives changes such as breast and uterine development.

records.question: A 40-year-old diabetic patient presented with the squint. On examination, the secondary deviation was found to be more than the primary deviation. Forced duction test is negative. Which of the following types of squint is most likely to be present in this patient?
records.explanation: A weak extraocular muscle can produce greater secondary than primary deviation, while a negative forced-duction test argues against mechanical restriction.

records.question: A 35 year old woman comes with complaints of warty lesions on the vulva. On examination, multiple warty growths on the vulva and around the anal canal are seen. This condition is most likely seen in?
records.explanation: HPV-associated condylomata are exophytic anogenital warts. They differ from the broad moist condylomata lata of secondary syphilis.

records.question: A physician observed the following finding in a small child who came for an eye exam. This finding is associated with which of the following conditions?
records.explanation: Hypermetropia can drive accommodative convergence and childhood esotropia.

records.question: Sympathetic ophthalmia is seen after ___________?
records.explanation: Penetrating ocular injury or surgery can trigger bilateral granulomatous inflammation through immune responses to ocular antigens. Both eyes require specialist evaluation.

records.question: A patient is planned to undergo hysteroscopic polypectomy using bipolar electrocautery. What is the ideal agent for distention ?
records.explanation: Isotonic saline conducts current and can be used with bipolar hysteroscopic electrosurgery. Fluid absorption and overload still require careful monitoring.

records.question: A patient presents with midline swelling in the neck Biopsy revealing Orphan Annie's eye nuclei is shown in the image below. What is the diagnosis?
records.explanation: Papillary thyroid carcinoma characteristically shows nuclear clearing, grooves and inclusions. These features require interpretation with architecture and the full specimen.

records.question: A patient presented with unilateral and bilateral abducent palsy. What is the most probable cause?
records.explanation: Cavernous-sinus disease can affect abducens function, but unilateral or bilateral sixth-nerve palsy has several causes. Associated cranial signs and imaging determine localisation.

records.question: A 51-year-old male patient came with complaints of hematuria to the clinic. On examination, he was normotensive and had pedal edema. Investigations revealed the patient had no glycosuria and had a creatinine of 9. His renal biopsy is shown below. Which of the following investigation should be done to identify the disease?
records.explanation: Linear basement-membrane IgG staining supports anti-GBM disease. The biopsy pattern and serology are needed before assigning this cause to severe renal dysfunction.

records.question: Which of the following is an inhibitor of DNA synthesis?
records.explanation: Mercaptopurine metabolites inhibit purine synthesis and can enter nucleic-acid pathways, impairing proliferation. Exposure and toxicity depend on metabolism and interacting drugs.

records.question: Large, friable, irregular vegetations on heart valves are seen in which condition?
records.explanation: Infective endocarditis can produce friable platelet-fibrin vegetations containing organisms and inflammatory material. Culture and clinical criteria distinguish noninfective vegetations.

records.question: A 23-year-old male patient presented with a history of fatigue and tiredness. On investigation, he was found to have Hb = 9 gm% MCV = 101 FL. Peripheral smear examination showed macrocytic RBC and hypersegmented neutrophils. Which of the following is the most likely etiology?
records.explanation: Alcohol can cause macrocytosis directly and through nutritional folate deficiency. Hypersegmented neutrophils suggest megaloblastosis; the blood film alone does not prove alcohol exposure.

records.question: A 52 year old woman diagnosed with carcinoma cervix stage 2B was advised radiotherapy. Which of the following statements regarding radiotherapy is false ?
options: Point B is 3 cm lateral to point A
Point A is 2 cm above the external os and 5cm lateral to the internal uterine canal
Point A receives a dose of 7000 cGy
Point B receives a dose of 6000 cGy
records.explanation: Traditional point A lies roughly two centimetres above the cervical reference point and two centimetres lateral to the uterine canal. Five centimetres lateral is not the conventional definition.

records.question: A 5-year-old child was admitted to the hospital with a history of prolapsing rectal mass and painless rectal bleeding. The histopathological image of the mass is shown below. What is the most likely diagnosis?
records.explanation: A juvenile polyp can cause painless rectal bleeding in children and shows cystically dilated glands in inflamed stroma. Histology confirms the pictured lesion.

records.question: A patient on lithium developed hypertension. He was started on thiazides for hypertension. After few days, he developed coarse tremors and other symptoms suggestive of lithium toxicity. Explain the likely mechanism of this interaction
options: Thiazide inhibits the metabolism of lithium
Thiazides act as an add on drug to lithium
Thiazides increase the tubular resorption of lithium
Thiazides cause water loss thereby increase lithium levels
records.explanation: Thiazide-related sodium depletion increases proximal lithium reabsorption and can raise lithium concentrations. Renal function, hydration and serum levels require assessment.

records.question: Which of the following should not be prescribed with theophylline?
records.explanation: Erythromycin can inhibit theophylline clearance and increase toxicity risk. Interaction magnitude depends on the specific macrolide, dose and clinical context.

records.question: Which of the following drugs gets deposited in the cornea?
records.explanation: Chloroquine can produce vortex-pattern corneal deposits. Corneal deposits must be distinguished from its potentially sight-threatening retinal toxicity.

records.question: A 20-year-old patient presented to the clinic with a history of malabsorption, diarrhea, and poor appetite. A duodenal biopsy of the patient showed crypt hyperplasia, villi atrophy, and CD8+ cells in lamina propria. What is the most probable diagnosis?
records.explanation: Villous atrophy, crypt hyperplasia and increased intraepithelial lymphocytes support coeliac disease.

records.question: A decreased male was brought to the morgue for a post-mortem examination. His relatives reported that he had a tattoo over his skin, which was not found on examination. Which of the following structures would you examine?
records.explanation: Macrophages can carry tattoo pigment to regional lymph nodes, where deposits may persist after the skin marking becomes difficult to see.

records.question: A patient was prescribed an antipsychotic drug following which he developed parkinsonism. Which of the following drugs can be given?
records.explanation: Trihexyphenidyl may relieve selected antipsychotic-induced parkinsonian symptoms. Reducing or changing the causative drug and anticholinergic risks require consideration.

records.question: A woman with a history of infertility is on treatment with human menopausal gonadotropin. She presented with the following finding in the USG. What is the most likely diagnosis ?
records.explanation: Gonadotropin stimulation can produce enlarged ovaries and increased vascular permeability with ascites. The ultrasound and systemic findings determine whether ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome is present.

records.question: Which section of the IPC deals with the punishment of perjury?
records.explanation: IPC section 193 historically prescribed punishment for false evidence. Preserve its historical exam context rather than treating the old number as current criminal-law advice.

records.question: A lady who is 38 weeks pregnant comes to the OPD for a routine checkup. She has a history of normal twin delivery at term 4 years ago. What is her gravida and para score ?
records.explanation: The current pregnancy makes gravida two, while the previous twin delivery counts as one pregnancy reaching the parity threshold. Thus G2P1 is appropriate.

records.question: The most common drug which causes physical dependence is?
records.explanation: Heroin can cause strong physical dependence, but a universal most-common dependence ranking needs a defined population and exposure pattern. Dependence differs from substance-use-disorder diagnosis.

records.question: Identify the finding seen in this hysterosalpingogram:
records.explanation: Distal tubal obstruction can dilate fluid-filled fallopian tubes. The HSG must demonstrate the retained bilateral pattern and distinguish other tubal abnormalities.

records.question: Which of the following antiarrhythmic drugs is contraindicated in a patient with interstitial lung disease?
records.explanation: Amiodarone can cause serious pulmonary toxicity. Pre-existing interstitial disease raises concern, but prescribing decisions depend on arrhythmia need, alternatives and specialist risk assessment.

records.question: A 5-year-old child with a history of perianal pain is brought to the OPD. On subjecting the specimen from the perianal region to a test, it produces yellow rhombic crystals of spermine picrate. What is the test done?
records.explanation: The historical Barberio test forms yellow spermine-picrate crystals from seminal constituents. It does not by itself prove sexual contact or abuse.

records.question: Which of the following drugs acts by inhibiting the late sodium current in the heart?
records.explanation: Ranolazine inhibits late cardiac sodium current, reducing associated intracellular calcium loading. It improves angina through a mechanism distinct from simple heart-rate reduction.

records.question: A 3-year-old child was brought to the hospital with complaints of fever, rash and swelling of her hands and feet since past 5 days. There is desquamative skin rash, oedema of hands and feet, erythema of palms and soles, oral erythema, and cervical lymphadenopathy. What is the likely condition?
records.explanation: Prolonged fever with mucocutaneous and extremity changes plus lymphadenopathy suggests Kawasaki disease. Diagnostic criteria and cardiac assessment determine treatment urgency.

records.question: Identify the maternal condition that can lead to the findings in the baby as shown below:
records.explanation: Poorly controlled pregestational diabetes increases congenital anomaly risk. The infant image must establish the intended anomaly; appearance alone does not classify maternal diabetes.

records.question: Effacement of podocyte foot processes is seen in which of the following diseases?
records.explanation: Diffuse foot-process effacement is characteristic of minimal-change disease but can occur in other podocytopathies. Light microscopy, immunofluorescence and clinical findings matter.

records.question: A woman with endometrial carcinoma is undergoing radiotherapy. Which of the following is true?
options: Intensity is inversely proportional to squared distance
Small blood vessels are most radioresistant
Rapidly proliferating cells are most radioresistant
records.explanation: For an ideal point source, intensity falls in proportion to the inverse square of distance. Real treatment geometry and attenuation require additional dosimetric considerations.

records.question: Thrombosis is initiated by:
records.explanation: Endothelial injury promotes thrombosis, alongside abnormal flow and hypercoagulability in Virchow's triad. It is not the sole initiating mechanism in every thrombus.

records.question: Identify the use of the instrument given below:
options: For ligation of uterine artery during hysterectomy
records.explanation: Instruments used for tubal sterilisation grasp or expose the tube. The specific photograph is needed before assigning this procedural use.

records.question: A patient with diabetes and COPD developed postoperative urinary retention. Which of the following drugs can be used for short-term treatment of the condition?
records.explanation: Bethanechol stimulates muscarinic receptors and can increase bladder contraction, but also risks bronchoconstriction. The stated obstructive lung disease makes an unqualified recommendation unsafe.

records.question: A middle-aged woman presents with thyroid swelling. Blood tests show elevated TSH levels and the presence of thyroid peroxidase antibodies. Histopathological examination revealed the presence of Hurthle cells. What is the most likely diagnosis?
records.explanation: Thyroid autoantibodies, hypothyroidism and lymphocytic inflammation with Hurthle cells support Hashimoto thyroiditis. Other thyroid conditions can share individual features.

records.question: All of the following are contraceptive methods used post – coitus except:
options: Combined high dose estrogen – progestin pills
records.explanation: Danazol is not a standard emergency contraceptive. Established emergency methods use selected hormonal medicines or an appropriate intrauterine device within recommended windows.

records.question: A 52-year-old male patient comes with complaints of abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. A peripheral blood smear reveals macrocytes and hypersegmented neutrophils and an endoscopy reveals atrophic gastritis. Which of the following conditions is likely to be seen this patient?
records.explanation: Autoimmune gastric parietal-cell loss reduces intrinsic factor and B12 absorption, causing megaloblastic anaemia and potentially neurological injury.

records.question: In the civil negligence case against a doctor who bears the onus of proof?
options: Police not under rank of sub-inspector
records.explanation: A claimant generally bears the burden of proving civil negligence, subject to evidential doctrines and case circumstances. The isolated option is not a complete legal standard.

records.question: A 35-year-old woman presents with a lump in the upper outer quadrant of her breast. Histopathological examination of the mass showed cells in mucin pools and faint nuclei. What is the most likely diagnosis?
records.explanation: Tumour cells floating within abundant extracellular mucin support mucinous, historically colloid, breast carcinoma. Histological classification requires the complete specimen.

records.question: A patient presented with pain in the hand. The joints involved were proximal interphalangeal joint, distal interphalangeal joint and first carpometacarpal joint. The wrist and metacarpophalangeal joints were spared. What is the likely diagnosis?
records.explanation: DIP, PIP and first carpometacarpal involvement with relative MCP sparing is a typical hand-osteoarthritis distribution, unlike classic rheumatoid arthritis.

records.question: A maid is playing with a child by spinning him while holding his hands. A few hours later, the child starts crying, does not use his arm, and does not let anybody touch him. What is the possible diagnosis?
records.explanation: Axial traction on a young child's extended arm can sublux the radial head relative to the annular ligament, causing painful refusal to use the arm.

records.question: Which of the following drugs is used for the treatment of motion sickness?
records.explanation: Promethazine's antihistamine and antimuscarinic effects can suppress vestibular nausea. Sedation and age-related safety restrictions affect its suitability.

records.question: What is the child-Turcotte-Pugh class for the patient who has a serum bilirubin 2.5 mg/dl, serum albumin 3 g/dl, prothrombin time 5 seconds (INR =2), no encephalopathy, and mild ascites?
records.explanation: Bilirubin, albumin, coagulation, ascites and encephalopathy are scored separately. The supplied values total within the seven-to-nine-point class B range using standard thresholds.

records.question: Which of the following is not a prokinetic?
records.explanation: Diphenylmethane derivatives are stimulant laxatives rather than standard upper-gastrointestinal prokinetic medicines. Drug class should be distinguished from any general increase in bowel activity.

records.question: Two girls in the same class are diagnosed with meningococcal meningitis. Their 12-year old friend from the same school is afraid of contracting the disease. What advice should be given to the exposed students?
records.explanation: Prophylaxis is indicated for qualifying close contacts, not automatically every classmate. Exposure definition and public-health investigation determine which students need treatment.

records.question: An elderly woman is brought to the OPD with complaints of behavioural change, a history of multiple falls, urinary incontinence, and dementia. What is your diagnosis?
records.explanation: Gait disturbance, cognitive decline and urinary symptoms suggest normal-pressure hydrocephalus. Imaging and appropriate assessment distinguish it from other causes of this nonspecific triad.

records.question: A 60-year-old male patient who is a known case of COPD presented with acute exacerbation and is admitted to the ICU. Which of the following statements is correct with regards to the initial management of this patient?
records.explanation: Noninvasive ventilation benefits selected acute COPD exacerbations with hypercapnic respiratory acidosis. Contraindications, consciousness and haemodynamic stability determine whether invasive support is needed.

records.question: Which of the following is used in the first-line management of postmenopausal osteoporosis?
records.explanation: Bisphosphonates are common initial antiresorptive options for suitable postmenopausal patients. Fracture risk, renal function and very-high-risk disease can change first treatment choice.

records.question: A laborer's second child is brought to the OPD with a swollen belly and dull face. He has been fed rice water (rice milk) in his diet mostly. On investigations, the child is found to have low serum protein and low albumin. What is the probable diagnosis?
records.explanation: Nutritional oedema supports oedematous severe malnutrition. Low albumin and abdominal distension alone are insufficient; bilateral pitting oedema and competing causes need assessment.

records.question: Thrombocytopenia, eczema and recurrent infections are seen in:
records.explanation: Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome combines eczema, immunodeficiency and thrombocytopenia, typically with small platelets. It is classically X-linked.

records.question: Which of the following is true about the pathogenesis of Hirschsprung disease?
options: Failure of migration of neural crest cells
