records.explanation: Fluorescein highlights corneal epithelial defects under cobalt-blue illumination. The staining pattern helps assess abrasion or ulceration but must be interpreted with the slit-lamp examination.

records.question: A 55-year-old male presented with verrucous carcinoma around the glans of the penis. Examination reveals that the inguinal lymph nodes are not enlarged. What is the appropriate management for this patient?
records.explanation: Partial penectomy can treat selected invasive penile cancers while preserving a functional stump. Verrucous histology, lesion extent and feasibility of organ-preserving treatment matter; absence of palpable nodes does not by itself dictate this operation.

records.question: Identify the procedure being performed in the image given below.
options: Intraosseous route access for giving IV fluids
records.explanation: Intraosseous access provides rapid vascular access through the marrow when timely intravenous access is difficult.

records.question: A diabetic patient presents with sudden-onset perineal pain. On examination, foul-smelling discharge, and necrotic tissue as seen in the image is noted. Which of the following is true about the given condition?
options: Anti-gas gangrene serum indicated for all cases
Urinary diversion is the next step
records.explanation: Fournier gangrene is a necrotising infection of perineal fascia and is often polymicrobial, involving aerobic and anaerobic organisms.

records.question: Which of the following is the most common complication following ligation of the first vessel during abdominoperineal resection for rectal carcinoma? (APR Abdominoperineal resection)
options: Sympathetic- retrograde ejaculation and bladder dysfunction.
Sympathetic-Impotence and loss of cutaneous sensation in perineal region
records.explanation: Sympathetic pathways contribute to emission and bladder-neck closure, so injury can cause ejaculatory dysfunction. Pelvic surgery can also damage parasympathetic pathways; the exact bladder and sexual deficit depends on the injured nerves.

records.question: A patient presents to the clinic with the lesion given in the image. He had a traumatic injury to the chest one year ago. What is the most likely diagnosis?
records.explanation: A keloid extends beyond the original wound boundary because of excessive scar formation.

records.question: A 45-year-old male underwent bilateral laparoscopic hernia repair for inguinal hernia. Postoperatively, he complained of pain in the right thigh. Which of the following nerve entrapment leads to this symptom?
records.explanation: The lateral femoral cutaneous nerve supplies sensation to the anterolateral thigh and can be injured near the lateral inguinal operative field. It is a sensory nerve, so isolated injury does not cause muscle weakness.

records.question: A patient was brought to the ER following a road traffic accident. On examination, the patient opens his eyes to a painful stimulus, speaks inappropriately, and withdraws his limbs to a painful stimulus. What is his GCS score?
records.explanation: Eye opening to pain scores 2, inappropriate words score 3 and withdrawal from pain scores 4. Their sum is 9; document the component scores as well as the total.

records.question: A patient presented with fever and abdominal pain with jaundice. Investigations showed the given findings. Which of the following statements is true regarding this condition?
options: Angioembolization is the treatment of choice
Echinococcus species is involved in etiology
records.explanation: Echinococcus granulosus can produce hydatid cysts with daughter cysts or detached membranes.

records.question: A patient who is a known case of alcohol dependence syndrome presents with sudden and unintentional weight loss. What is the most likely diagnosis? -ALP 240 IU/L -S. Direct bilirubin - 1 mg/dL -AST/ALT -0.5 -Alpha fetoprotein- 600 ng/mL
records.explanation: Hepatocellular carcinoma is associated with chronic liver disease, and alpha-fetoprotein can be elevated. AFP alone is neither sufficiently sensitive nor specific; diagnosis depends on appropriate imaging and sometimes tissue assessment.

records.question: A lady developed a skin reaction, as shown in the image, after using a hair dye. Which of the following chemicals is responsible for this condition?
records.explanation: Para-phenylenediamine in hair dyes can cause delayed allergic contact dermatitis. The distribution, exposure history and sometimes patch testing are needed to distinguish it from irritant reactions and other eruptions.

records.question: A female patient presented with acne that is not resolving on oral isotretinoin and antibiotics therapy. Which of the following is the next best investigation?
records.explanation: Persistent severe acne accompanied by menstrual disturbance, hirsutism or virilisation warrants assessment for androgen excess. Resistant acne alone does not establish an endocrine disorder or justify the same hormone panel in everyone.

records.question: Identify the maneuver being performed in the given image.
records.explanation: Head tilt with chin lift opens the airway by moving the tongue away from the posterior pharynx in an unresponsive patient without suspected cervical injury.

records.question: A patient presented with features of chronic pancreatitis with recurrent attacks and has a 10 mm dilatation of the pancreatic duct with intraductal calculi present. Which of the following is the surgery of choice?
records.explanation: A longitudinal pancreaticojejunostomy can decompress a substantially dilated pancreatic duct in selected painful chronic pancreatitis. Duct anatomy, inflammatory head mass and other complications determine the appropriate operation.

records.question: A young woman complains of a painless ulcer in the genital area. It is associated with non-tender inguinal lymphadenopathy. What is the most likely diagnosis?
records.explanation: A primary syphilitic chancre is classically painless with relatively non-tender regional nodes. Clinical appearances vary, so laboratory testing is needed rather than relying on pain alone.

records.question: Which of the following is associated with the clinical condition shown in the image?
records.explanation: Melanoma suspicion increases with asymmetry, irregular borders, colour variation and evolution.

records.question: Which of the following is the drug of choice for preoperative antibiotic prophylaxis in a patient undergoing cardiac surgery?
records.explanation: Cefazolin commonly provides prophylactic coverage for skin flora in cardiac surgery. Timing, redosing, allergy, colonisation and local resistance patterns determine the actual regimen; prophylaxis is distinct from treatment of established infection.

records.question: A 30-year-old male presents with nonaxial proptosis of the left eye. The patient gives a history of a road traffic accident 15 years back. The CT image is given below. What is the most likely diagnosis?
records.explanation: A frontal sinus mucocele can expand, erode surrounding bone and displace the orbit, sometimes after trauma or impaired drainage. CT location and expansion pattern are needed to support this diagnosis.

records.question: A woman presented with a BIRADS-5 breast lesion. Which of the following is a good prognostic factor for this lesion?
records.explanation: Oestrogen receptor expression predicts potential benefit from endocrine treatment and is often associated with more favourable tumour biology. It is a tissue biomarker, not an imaging substitute or an assurance of outcome in an individual patient.

records.question: A 55-year-old patient comes with hoarseness of voice and difficulty swallowing. The patient was diagnosed with laryngeal carcinoma, and surgical management was done. The post-operative image of the patient is given below. Which of the following surgery was done on this patient?
records.explanation: After total laryngectomy the airway is separated from the mouth and nose and opens through a permanent neck stoma.

records.question: A patient presents with sudden onset of chest pain shooting to the neck and interscapular region. X-ray shows widened mediastinum. BP is 110/90 mmHg in the right upper limb and 160/100 mmHg in the left upper limb. What is the most likely diagnosis?
records.explanation: Abrupt severe chest or back pain with pulse or blood-pressure asymmetry raises concern for aortic dissection. Urgent imaging and stabilisation are needed; symptoms alone do not identify the involved aortic segment.

records.question: A female patient with hearing loss is examined and is found to be Rinne negative at 256 Hz and 512 Hz, while Rinne positive at 1024 Hz. What is the expected air conduction and bone conduction gap?
records.explanation: A negative Rinne test suggests sufficiently large conductive hearing loss, but the threshold varies with fork frequency and technique. An exact air-bone gap should be measured by audiometry rather than inferred precisely from a tuning-fork result.

records.question: A patient presented with right hypochondriac pain. He had an episode of diarrhea 1 week prior. CT scan of the abdomen reveals a liver abscess of around 25 ccs. What is the next step in management?
records.explanation: A small uncomplicated amoebic liver abscess often responds to a tissue-active drug followed by a luminal agent. Prior diarrhoea is not proof of amoebiasis; pyogenic abscesses require a different microbiological and drainage assessment.

records.question: A child was brought with bony deformities, as shown in the radiograph below. It could be due to the deficiency of which of the following?
records.explanation: Vitamin D deficiency can impair growth-plate mineralisation and produce metaphyseal cupping and fraying.

records.question: A 50-year-old patient with a history of trauma one week back presents with confusion and ataxia. He is on treatment for alcohol dependence and his last intake was 2 weeks back. CT scan reveals the following finding. What is the diagnosis?
records.explanation: A subdural haematoma typically forms a crescent-shaped extra-axial collection from bleeding between dura and arachnoid.

records.question: Which of the following is false about the given condition?
options: Repeated radical surgery every 24 hours may be required to adequately manage this condition
This is a case of Meleney's gangrene
The condition is caused by β hemolytic streptococcus and may sometimes be polymicrobial
Hyperbaric oxygen has no role in the treatment of this condition
records.explanation: Urgent debridement and antimicrobial treatment are central to necrotising infection management.

records.question: A bronchial asthma patient on inhalational steroids presented with white patchy lesions on the tongue and buccal mucosa. What is the drug that can be used to treat this condition?
records.explanation: Inhaled corticosteroids can predispose to oral candidiasis through local immunosuppression. Topical antifungals such as clotrimazole may treat uncomplicated disease; inhaler technique and mouth rinsing reduce recurrence risk.

records.question: A patient presents with a swelling in the groin region and it is diagnosed as a direct inguinal hernia. Weakness in which of the following structures is most likely to cause this condition?
records.explanation: A direct inguinal hernia protrudes through weakness of the posterior inguinal wall in Hesselbach's triangle. Transversalis fascia is fundamental to that wall; the conjoint tendon reinforces it medially, so attributing all direct hernias simply to tendon weakness is incomplete.

records.question: A pregnant woman with a history of bronchial asthma is in the third stage of labor. Which drugs should be avoided in managing postpartum hemorrhage in this mother?
records.explanation: Carboprost is a prostaglandin F2-alpha analogue that contracts uterine smooth muscle but can also cause bronchoconstriction. Asthma therefore materially affects its suitability for postpartum haemorrhage treatment.

records.question: In which of the following nerve injuries is the instrument shown below used?
records.explanation: The radial nerve is vulnerable along the humeral shaft and during relevant instrumentation.

records.question: Name the drug that acts on both the marked areas.
records.explanation: Omapatrilat inhibits both angiotensin-converting enzyme and neprilysin. Increased bradykinin-related angioedema limited its clinical development; its mechanism should not be confused with currently used angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitor combinations.

records.question: A patient presented with chronic knee pain but has no history of trauma. Identify the condition shown in the radiograph below and the appropriate management.
options: Bipartite fracture patella, X-ray of other knees
Fracture of the upper pole of the patella, Cylindrical cast
records.explanation: A bipartite patella is a developmental accessory ossification pattern, commonly with a well-corticated superolateral fragment. Contralateral imaging may support the diagnosis, but it is not itself a patellar fracture and must be distinguished from acute injury.

records.question: A construction worker came to the OPD complaining of white fingers. He has been working in the cement and concrete industry and has been working on heavy machinery drills, wood, and furniture polishing for 20 years. What is the most likely etiology for this condition?
options: Candidal infection of the fingers due to continuous exposure to water
Continuous exposure to cement and concrete
Continuous exposure to drills and machines
records.explanation: Repeated hand-arm vibration can cause episodic digital vasospasm and sensory symptoms. Cold-triggered blanching in an exposed worker supports vibration-related vascular disease, while other causes of Raynaud phenomenon remain possible.

records.question: A patient with a previous history of myocardial infarction and ventricular arrhythmia is on treatment for a few months. He developed fatigue, dyspnea, and weight gain. He had also developed pulmonary fibrosis. Which of the following drugs is responsible for the side effects mentioned above?
records.explanation: Amiodarone can produce pulmonary toxicity and thyroid dysfunction through several mechanisms, including its iodine content and tissue accumulation. Respiratory symptoms require evaluation because infection and heart failure can resemble drug toxicity.

records.question: A 5-year-old child was admitted to the hospital for prolapsing rectal mass and painless rectal bleeding. Histopathological examination reveals enlarged and inflamed glands filled with mucin. What is the likely diagnosis?
records.explanation: A juvenile polyp is a hamartomatous lesion with cystically dilated, mucus-filled glands in an inflamed stroma. A solitary juvenile polyp differs in risk and management from a hereditary polyposis syndrome.

records.question: A young female comes to the emergency department after consuming 100 aspirin tablets. What should be the next step in management?
options: N-acetyl cysteine to replenish glutathione stores
Glucagon to control bradycardia and hypoglycemia
Give sodium bicarbonate to alkalize urine
records.explanation: Intravenous bicarbonate can enhance salicylate elimination by alkalinising urine and can help limit tissue distribution. Severe toxicity may require haemodialysis; clinical status, acid-base balance, renal function and measured levels govern management rather than tablet count alone.

records.question: A chronic smoker was on nicotine replacement therapy and clonidine tablets for smoking de-addiction. He stopped taking clonidine tablets and now presents with a headache. What is the reason behind this condition?
records.explanation: Abrupt withdrawal of clonidine can cause rebound sympathetic activation and severe hypertension. Its central alpha-2 agonist effect normally suppresses sympathetic outflow.

records.question: Identify the given condition.
records.explanation: Loss of protective sensation allows repeated unnoticed pressure injury and can produce a neuropathic ulcer.

records.question: A patient with recurrent gout attacks was started on a therapy that inhibits uric acid synthesis. His symptoms were reduced after therapy. Which drug was he started on?
records.explanation: Allopurinol and its active metabolite inhibit xanthine oxidase, reducing uric acid formation. It is urate-lowering treatment rather than immediate analgesia for an acute gout attack.

records.question: A patient with a malignancy is undergoing chemotherapy. The platelet counts were reduced after the previous cycle of chemotherapy. Which of the following drugs can be used to treat this patient?
records.explanation: Oprelvekin is recombinant interleukin-11 and promotes megakaryocyte maturation and platelet production. Its historical thrombocytopenia indication should not be treated as a universal or current first-line approach to low platelet counts.

records.question: The true statement among the following is___
options: The dose of telmisartan should be reduced in renal failure but not in hepatic failure.
The dose of irbesartan should be reduced in case of mild-moderate hepatic failure and renal failure.
The dose of candesartan should be reduced in mild-moderate liver failure but not in renal failure.
Losartan acts as a thromboxane A2 antagonist and inhibits platelet aggregation.
records.explanation: Losartan's established therapeutic mechanism is angiotensin II AT1 receptor blockade. Experimental antiplatelet effects involving thromboxane pathways have been described, but this ancillary observation must not be interpreted as a clinical antiplatelet indication or substitute for standard antithrombotic treatment.

records.question: A child is brought to the orthopedics OPD with a deformity in the lower limb and hyperpigmented skin lesions. The x-ray of her thigh is shown below. What is the most likely diagnosis?
records.explanation: Fibrous dysplasia replaces normal bone with fibro-osseous tissue. Its combination with characteristic pigmentation and endocrine hyperfunction suggests McCune-Albright syndrome; pigmentation alone does not establish the full syndrome.

records.question: A schizophrenic patient was prescribed drug A after he did not respond to haloperidol and thioridazine. He now presents with excessive salivation, an increase in blood glucose, and hyperlipidemia. What is drug A?
records.explanation: Clozapine is used for appropriately established treatment-resistant schizophrenia and can cause hypersalivation and metabolic adverse effects. Serious blood and cardiac adverse effects require structured monitoring.

records.question: The given image is an x-ray of a 22-year-old female. What is the probable diagnosis?
records.explanation: A giant cell tumour typically occurs near the joint in an epiphysis after skeletal maturity.

records.question: Identify the marked region in the given spirometry.
records.explanation: Functional residual capacity equals expiratory reserve volume plus residual volume.

records.question: A patient with varicose veins complains of eczema over the same region. What is the stage of the clinical classification according to the CEAP guidelines? CEAP-Clinical-Aetiology-Anatomy- Pathophysiology classification of chronic venous disorders
records.explanation: In the CEAP clinical classification, C4a includes pigmentation or eczema related to chronic venous disease. An active ulcer is classified separately rather than included merely as eczema.

records.question: A patient comes to the casualty with a severe headache. His BP was found to be 160/100 mmHg. CT scan revealed a subarachnoid hemorrhage. What is the next best step in the management of this patient?
records.explanation: Vascular imaging can identify an aneurysm after subarachnoid haemorrhage and guide definitive treatment. Angiography is part of urgent specialist assessment, not a substitute for stabilisation or management of complications.

records.question: Identify the correctly matched pair of substances with their renal clearance from the graph below.
options: A-Glucose, B-PAH, C- Bicarbonate and D - Inulin
A-Glucose, B- Bicarbonate, C-Inulin and D - PAH
A-PAH, B-Inulin, C - Glucose and D - Bicarbonate
A - Inulin, B - Glucose, C - Bicarbonate and D - PAH
records.explanation: Clearance is urinary concentration times urine flow divided by plasma concentration. Inulin approximates GFR, PAH approximates effective renal plasma flow under appropriate conditions, and normally reabsorbed glucose has near-zero clearance; assigning the graph labels needs the image.

records.question: A 20-year-old female patient consumed a cleaning product containing 90% sodium hydroxide. She is having complete dysphagia. What is the best step in management?
records.explanation: A feeding jejunostomy may provide nutrition in selected severe oesophageal injury or later obstruction. It is not the automatic first step after caustic ingestion; airway, perforation risk, injury assessment and specialist planning take priority.

records.question: A 23-year-old male patient presents with midline swelling in the neck. The swelling moves with deglutition and protrusion of the tongue. What is the likely diagnosis?
records.explanation: A thyroglossal duct cyst often moves with swallowing and tongue protrusion because of its attachment along the embryological thyroid descent tract. Ultrasound helps confirm normal thyroid tissue and evaluate the mass.

records.question: Identify the true statement regarding the given nerve action potential curve?
options: The threshold point is at A
At point E, the nerve is more excitable
Point C to D is due to the opening of Na+ and closure of K+ channels
Point B to D is a refractory period
records.explanation: Refractoriness follows sodium-channel inactivation and changes during repolarisation.

records.question: A young patient is admitted with a history of fever for 5 days. BP is 90/60 mmHg, PR-120 bpm, RR-24 breaths/ min, GCS score-10; laboratory tests show leucocytosis with neutrophilia and serum creatinine level of 2.6 mg/ dL. An intern doctor wants to calculate the qSOFA score to predict prognosis and hospitalization duration. Which of the following comprises the qSOFA score?
records.explanation: qSOFA assigns one point each for systolic pressure at or below 100 mmHg, respiratory rate at least 22 per minute and altered mentation. These values give a total of 3 and indicate increased risk in suspected infection.

records.question: Identify the type of transport across the cell membrane given below?
records.explanation: Facilitated diffusion moves solute down its electrochemical gradient through a membrane protein without directly consuming metabolic energy.

records.question: Identify the condition associated with the murmur in the image below.
records.explanation: Mitral regurgitation typically causes a systolic murmur, often heard best at the apex with radiation toward the axilla.

records.question: A 25-year-old female reported symptoms of anxiety, palpitations, sweating, breathlessness, chest pain, and a feeling of impending doom. She recalls having experienced 5-6 similar episodes in the past 6 months, each episode lasting for about 20-30 minutes. What is the likely diagnosis?
records.explanation: Panic attacks are abrupt surges of intense fear with physical symptoms. Panic disorder additionally requires recurrent unexpected attacks and persistent concern or maladaptive behaviour; a brief attack description alone does not establish all criteria.

records.question: A young man came to the medical OPD with complaints of early morning backache and stiffness, which improves on exercise, and persistent red eyes. On examination, lung expansion was less than 3 cm. X-ray is shown in the image given below. What is the most probable diagnosis?
records.explanation: Inflammatory back pain associated with anterior uveitis supports a spondyloarthritis diagnosis. Imaging, examination and clinical criteria are needed; neither an eye image nor HLA-B27 alone establishes ankylosing spondylitis.

records.question: A patient with hyperkalemia and elevated urea levels underwent dialysis. Towards the end of the session, she became drowsy and had a sudden seizure episode. On examination, the patient was hypotensive. What is the treatment for this condition?
records.explanation: Rapid osmotic change during dialysis can cause cerebral oedema, headache, confusion or seizures, termed dialysis disequilibrium syndrome. Seizure with hypotension also requires immediate assessment for hypoglycaemia, electrolyte disturbance and other emergencies; mannitol is not an automatic diagnosis-independent response.

records.question: A female patient presents to the emergency department with severe restlessness, palpitations, and tremors. She is a known case of bronchial asthma. On examination, the neck looks swollen. Blood pressure is elevated, and tachycardia is noted. ECG shows atrial fibrillation. Which of the following drugs is used for immediate management in this patient?
records.explanation: Diltiazem can reduce ventricular rate when beta blockade is unsuitable, including selected patients with bronchospasm. Cardiac function and haemodynamics matter, and rate control does not treat the underlying thyroid hormone excess.

records.question: A preterm baby who was delivered at 28 weeks developed respiratory distress syndrome. Which of the following is true about surface tension and compliance in this baby?
options: Both surface tension and compliance decreased
Both surface tension and compliance increased
records.explanation: Pulmonary surfactant lowers alveolar surface tension. Deficiency increases the pressure needed to inflate alveoli, reduces compliance and favours collapse.

records.question: A middle-aged man complains of very early ejaculation during intercourse. What is the non-pharmacological management that can be advised to the patient?
records.explanation: The squeeze technique is a behavioural method intended to interrupt increasing arousal before ejaculation. Treatment should be individualised after assessing distress, timing, relationship factors and possible associated disorders.

records.question: A 30-year-old male is found to be positive for HBsAg and HBeAg and is diagnosed with chronic hepatitis B. The patient’s viral load was 2x 100000 and SGPT is found to be doubled. What is the appropriate management in this patient? SGPT-Serum glutamate pyruvate transaminase
records.explanation: Tenofovir is a potent antiviral option for eligible chronic hepatitis B patients. Treatment duration is not a standard 40-week course: many patients need prolonged therapy, and stopping depends on virological, serological and liver-disease criteria with follow-up.

records.question: A 25-year-old male patient complained of palpitations, sweating, and restlessness. He has a complaint of sweaty palms. Clinical findings are depicted in the image given below. What is the diagnostic test done on this patient?
records.explanation: Thyrotropin receptor antibodies can stimulate the thyroid and support Graves disease.

records.question: A 50-year-old HIV patient presented with a painless lesion, as shown in the image. What is the most likely diagnosis?
records.explanation: Kaposi sarcoma is associated with human herpesvirus 8 and can occur with advanced HIV-related immunosuppression.

records.question: A patient came to the hospital after a road traffic accident. He had severe muscle injury, and his serum K+ level was found to be 5.5 mEq/L. What will happen to the resting membrane potential in this patient?
options: First becomes more positive then negative
records.explanation: Increasing extracellular potassium reduces the transmembrane potassium gradient and generally makes the resting membrane potential less negative. Severe elevation can inactivate sodium channels and impair excitability rather than simply increasing it indefinitely.

records.question: A newborn presented with chest retractions, dyspnea, and lethargy. The pediatrician diagnosed the baby with respiratory distress syndrome. This occurs due to the deficiency of:
records.explanation: Dipalmitoylphosphatidylcholine, a lecithin, is a major surface-active component of pulmonary surfactant. Surfactant proteins and other lipids also contribute to its function.

records.question: A patient is brought to the OPD by his wife, complaining about difficulty expressing emotions and not participating in daily activities. On examination, resting tremors and rigidity are noted. Given the possible diagnosis, which part of the brain is affected in this patient?
records.explanation: Degeneration of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra pars compacta alters basal ganglia motor circuits. Parkinsonism reflects this network dysfunction rather than a generic loss of all basal ganglia neurons.

records.question: A patient met with a road traffic accident and developed a cervical spine injury. The fracture fragment had pierced the lateral aspect of the dorsal column tract. Which of the following findings is seen in this patient?
options: Absence of ipsilateral lower limb proprioception
Absence of fine motor movement of fingers
Absence of contralateral lower limb proprioception
records.explanation: The fasciculus cuneatus carries ipsilateral upper-body vibration, discriminative touch and proprioception in the spinal cord before crossing in the medulla. It lies lateral to the gracile fasciculus in the dorsal columns.

records.question: A male patient presented to the emergency room with seizures. He has a history of fever, headache, and confusion. An MRI brain was done, and it showed inflammation involving the bitemporal lobe. What is the most likely aetiology for this presentation?
records.explanation: Herpes simplex encephalitis often affects temporal and inferior frontal regions and can cause fever, seizures and altered behaviour. The distribution is suggestive rather than exclusive, and urgent antiviral treatment should accompany diagnostic assessment.

records.question: Identify the true statement regarding the point marked(Red) on the myocardial action potential curve?
options: Due to the opening of Na+ and closure of fast K+ channels
Due to the slow but prolonged opening of Ca2+ channels
Due to the closure of Na+ and opening of the slow K+ channel
records.explanation: L-type calcium entry contributes to the plateau of a ventricular myocyte action potential while potassium currents also influence its duration.

records.question: A male patient presents with sensory loss and weakness of limbs for 3 months. He also has angular stomatitis. On examination, there is loss of proprioception, vibration sensations, UMN type of lower limb weakness, and absent ankle reflex. What is the most probable diagnosis?
records.explanation: Vitamin B12 deficiency can injure dorsal columns and corticospinal tracts, causing impaired position sense with upper motor neuron signs. Neurological disease can occur without marked anaemia.

records.question: A 10-year-old child weighing 30 kg presents with a history of loose stools for 2 days. On examination, there is severe dehydration. Laboratory investigations are as follows. What is the initial management as per ISPAD guidelines? RBS 550mg/dL pH 7.01 Na+ 158mEq/L Urine glucose 3+
options: Manage ABC, NS 20 mL/kg and start insulin after 1 hour
Manage ABC, NS 20 mL/kg along with insulin 0.1 IU/kg/hr
Manage ABC, NS 10 mL/kg along with insulin 0.1 IU/kg/hr
Manage ABC, NS 10 mL/kg and start insulin after 1 hour
records.explanation: Paediatric DKA treatment uses controlled fluid replacement, insulin after initial fluids and careful potassium and glucose monitoring. Fluid requirements depend on perfusion, dehydration and the clinical protocol.

records.question: Which of the following is the best sign to indicate adequate growth in an infant with a birth weight of 2.8 kg?
options: Increase in length of 25 centimetres in the first year
Weight gain of 300 grams per month till 1 year
Anterior fontanelle closure by 6 months of age
Weight under the 75th percentile and height under the 25th percentile
records.explanation: Length increases by approximately 25 cm during the first year in a typically growing term infant. This is a population teaching estimate, and serial measurements on a growth chart assess an individual child.

records.question: A 40-year-old female patient came with complaints of chest pain, palpitation, and shortness of breath. On examination, a mid-diastolic murmur was heard, and a prominent 'a' wave was found on JVP. What is the most likely diagnosis?
records.explanation: Tricuspid stenosis impedes right atrial emptying, producing a prominent jugular a wave when sinus rhythm is present and a diastolic inflow murmur. Atrial fibrillation removes organised a waves.

records.question: A 3-month-old baby complains of deafness, cataract, and patent ductus arteriosus. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
records.explanation: Congenital rubella can cause cataracts, sensorineural hearing loss and cardiac lesions such as patent ductus arteriosus. Maternal and infant testing and exposure timing support confirmation.

records.question: Research is being conducted to find the association between aniline dye exposure and bladder cancer in workers who have worked in the industry for >20 years. Two groups were formed: one directly involved with dye handling and the other group consisting of office clerks not directly exposed to the dye. Years of occupation were noted from records. What type of study is being performed?
records.explanation: A cohort study compares subsequent disease occurrence in exposed and unexposed groups. It is retrospective when both exposure and outcome are reconstructed from existing records; an occupational exposure alone does not determine the study's time direction.

records.question: Chloride level in sweat is used in the diagnosis of which disease?
records.explanation: Elevated sweat chloride reflects defective CFTR-mediated chloride handling and supports cystic fibrosis diagnosis under standardised testing conditions. Borderline or discordant results require further evaluation, not automatic confirmation.

records.question: A child presents with fever and a rash spreading from the face, behind cheeks, and buccal mucosa to other body parts. On examination, Koplik's spot is present. What is the likely diagnosis?
records.explanation: Koplik spots are small pale lesions on an erythematous buccal background associated with measles. Suspected measles also requires appropriate infection control and public-health testing.

records.question: The blood pressure of a population was tracked from childhood to adulthood. It was observed that those who had lower BP in childhood had low BP in adulthood, while those who had higher BP in childhood had high BP in adulthood. This can be best described as
records.explanation: Tracking describes the tendency for a person's relative blood-pressure position within a population to persist over time. It is a statistical tendency, not certainty that an individual child will develop adult hypertension.

records.question: A 3-week-old infant presents with a cough and sore throat. The mother reports that the infant develops a paroxysm of cough followed by apnea. The total leucocyte count is >50,000 cells/μL. Which of the following drugs will you prescribe for this patient?
records.explanation: Pertussis can cause apnoea and marked lymphocytosis in young infants even without a typical whoop. Azithromycin is used in this setting, while respiratory support and age-specific monitoring remain essential.

records.question: A 30-week primigravida complaints of reduced vision at night. She has been avoiding papaya, mango, and other fruits throughout her pregnancy as she thinks they could be abortifacients. It is the primary duty of which of the following workers to provide counseling and information to the patient?
records.explanation: ASHA workers support community counselling, linkage to care and follow-up for maternal nutrition concerns. Night blindness in pregnancy needs assessment and appropriate programme-based treatment; responsibility is shared across the health team.

records.question: Identify the structure marked in the image.
records.explanation: The pharyngeal recess behind the tubal elevation is the fossa of Rosenmuller, an important site for nasopharyngeal carcinoma.

records.question: A 22-year-old female comes to the STI clinic with minimal vaginal discharge. On speculum examination, erosions are seen on the cervix. Which of the following kit should be given to this patient?
records.explanation: Colour-coded STI kits group medicines for syndromic treatment under a national programme. The grey-kit association belongs to the relevant programme edition; antimicrobial regimens depend on the applicable guidance.

records.question: The years of potential life lost could be attributed to,
options: Years lost due to premature death
Years lost to poor quality of life
records.explanation: Years of potential life lost sums the gap between age at death and a chosen reference age for deaths before that threshold. It gives greater weight to premature mortality and depends on the chosen age convention.

records.question: The instrument shown in the image is not used for which of the following?
records.explanation: Identifying which instrument is unsuitable for an upper-airway examination requires its actual appearance and intended use.

records.question: In a 10-year-old school child, which of the following vaccines is given as a part of the school immunization program?
records.explanation: India's routine immunisation programme includes a Td dose at 10 years and another at 16 years. Vaccine choice and catch-up schedules should follow the applicable programme rather than assuming all countries use identical ages.

records.question: A 10-year-old child presents with throat pain, fever, and ear pain. He is diagnosed with recurrent tonsillitis. Which nerve is responsible for the ear pain in this patient?
options: Tympanic branch of the glossopharyngeal nerve
Auricular branch of the vagus nerve
records.explanation: The glossopharyngeal nerve supplies the tonsillar region and contributes to middle-ear sensation through its tympanic branch. Shared sensory pathways help explain referred ear pain from oropharyngeal disease.

records.question: Which of the following statements is true about cancer treatment according to the Colombo plan?
options: Help with PET scan units for diagnosis of cancer
records.explanation: The Colombo Plan supported international technical cooperation, including historical health-service development. This is a programme-history association, not a biological explanation for cobalt radiotherapy.

records.question: A poor farmer with a history of successive crop failure develops progressive spastic paraparesis, signs of upper motor neuron paralysis, and gait instability. Name the toxin responsible for this condition.
records.explanation: Grass pea contains beta-N-oxalyl-L-alpha,beta-diaminopropionic acid, often abbreviated ODAP or BOAA. Sustained heavy exposure in a nutritionally vulnerable population is associated with neurolathyrism and spastic paraparesis.

records.question: A young male came to the hospital with a clean-cut wound without any bleeding. The patient received a full course of tetanus vaccination 10 years ago. What is the best management for this patient?
options: Human tetanus immunoglobulin and full course of vaccine
records.explanation: For a clean minor wound in someone with a completed primary series, a booster is generally considered when at least 10 years have elapsed since the last tetanus-containing dose. Dirty or major wounds and incomplete histories use different rules.

records.question: How is water collected for bacteriological examination during a disease outbreak?
options: Collect water from already leaking taps
Before collecting, let water flow for at least 1 minute
Water sample container is kept close to the tap avoid spillage
Collect from a gentle stream of water to avoid splashing
records.explanation: Microbiological water sampling requires an appropriate sterile container and aseptic handling, with site-specific tap preparation and collection procedure. Instructions for a tap sample should not be generalised to every water source or chemical analysis.

records.question: A boys' hostel has an outbreak of fever cases with headache, followed by the development of pleomorphic rashes sparing palms and soles. What is the next best step in the management of suspected cases? VZIG-Varicella zoster immunoglobulin
options: Isolate for 6 days after giving acyclovir, followed by VZIG within 72 hours of exposure.
Isolate for 12 days after giving acyclovir, followed by VZIG within 48 hours of exposure
records.explanation: Varicella precautions continue until lesions have crusted; the timing varies and is commonly several days after rash onset. A fixed six-day rule should not replace checking the lesion stage and the applicable guidance.

records.question: A patient who is a known case of hypertension on multiple anti-hypertensive medications came to OPD. His ECG finding is given below. Which of the following drugs is responsible for the ECG finding?
records.explanation: Spironolactone reduces aldosterone-mediated potassium excretion and can cause hyperkalaemia. The missing ECG cannot establish the rhythm or severity, and serum testing and urgent assessment guide treatment.

records.question: A 78-year-old woman presents with a progressive decline in daily activity. She gives a history of convulsions and visual hallucinations. She does not talk to anyone and keeps looking at the sky. Pathological examination shows the presence of Lewy bodies within the neurons. What is the most probable diagnosis?
records.explanation: Lewy bodies contain abnormal alpha-synuclein and occur in Parkinson disease and dementia with Lewy bodies.

records.question: A patient came to the medical OPD with complaints of polyuria. He has a history of undergoing total hypophysectomy. His Na+ levels are found to be 155 mEq/ L, urine osmolarity was 200 mOsm/L. What is the definitive management in this patient?
options: DDAVP for 2 weeks and then discontinue
Upsetting of receptors so no treatment is required
records.explanation: Desmopressin replaces antidiuretic activity in central diabetes insipidus after pituitary injury. Postoperative dysfunction can be transient or permanent, so ongoing need depends on urine output, sodium and supervised reassessment.

records.question: A 65-year-old chronic smoker came to the medicine outpatient department with complaints of upper chest discomfort and drooping of an eyelid. He also complained of pain radiating to the upper arm and a tingling sensation in the 4th and 5th digits of his left hand. The chest X-ray is given below. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
records.explanation: An apical lung tumour can invade lower brachial plexus structures and the sympathetic chain, causing shoulder or arm pain with Horner syndrome. Imaging and tissue diagnosis are needed to define the lesion and stage.

records.question: A chronic alcoholic patient presents with acute pain and swelling of the left great toe. There is no history of trauma. Synovial fluid analysis shows raised leukocytes. Lab investigations show normal serum uric acid levels. What is the most likely diagnosis?
records.explanation: Serum urate may be normal during an acute gout attack. Synovial fluid identification of negatively birefringent monosodium urate crystals supports diagnosis, while infection must still be considered where clinically indicated.

records.question: A chronic alcoholic is brought to the emergency department with confusion, ataxia, and painful eye movements. The 6th cranial nerve is also involved. What is the likely diagnosis?
records.explanation: Thiamine deficiency disrupts energy metabolism in vulnerable brain regions and can cause confusion, gait ataxia and ocular abnormalities. Suspected Wernicke encephalopathy warrants prompt treatment without requiring every classic sign.

records.question: A patient given digoxin started having side effects like nausea and vomiting. The serum concentration of digoxin was 4 mg/dL. The plasma therapeutic range is 1 mg/dL. If the half-life of digoxin is 40 hours, how long should one wait before resuming the treatment?
records.explanation: With first-order elimination, a concentration fall from 4 to 1 requires two half-lives: 4 becomes 2, then 1. Two 40-hour half-lives equal 80 hours.

records.question: A patient comes to the casualty with organophosphate poisoning. He was started on atropine infusion and pralidoxime. After 2 hours, the patient had a sudden rise in temperature. What is the likely cause of fever?
records.explanation: Atropine can reduce sweating through muscarinic blockade and contribute to hyperthermia, especially with other anticholinergic signs. Fever in a poisoned patient also has other causes, so it should not automatically be attributed to atropine alone.

records.question: A partogram of a woman who is in labor is shown below. Oxytocin infusion is already given. How will you manage the condition?
records.explanation: A partograph requires the actual plotted cervical dilatation, time, contractions and maternal-fetal observations.

records.question: The mechanism of action of tissue plasminogen activator is
records.explanation: Tissue plasminogen activator promotes conversion of plasminogen to plasmin, which degrades fibrin. Clinical thrombolysis requires indication-specific eligibility and bleeding-risk assessment rather than mechanism alone.

records.question: A woman presents to you at 36 weeks of gestation with complaints of breathlessness and excessive abdominal distension. Fetal movements are normal. On examination, fetal parts are not easily felt and fetal heartbeat is heard but it is muffled. Her symphysis fundal height is 41 cm. Her abdomen is tense but not tender. What is the most likely diagnosis?
records.explanation: Excess amniotic fluid can enlarge the uterus and make fetal parts difficult to palpate. Ultrasound measurement is needed to confirm polyhydramnios and assess possible maternal or fetal causes.

records.question: For which of the following procedures in the given OT list, can you preferably do a hysteroscopy?
records.explanation: Hysteroscopy directly visualises intrauterine adhesions and can permit treatment in Asherman syndrome. The diagnosis should be linked to the menstrual, fertility and uterine instrumentation history.

records.question: A 23-year-old woman accompanied by her mother-in-law comes to the infertility clinic. She has been having regular intercourse for 6 months but is not able to conceive. What is the next best step?
options: Reassure and review the couple after 6 months
records.explanation: For a younger couple without recognised risk factors, evaluation is commonly initiated after 12 months of regular unprotected intercourse. Earlier assessment is appropriate with risk factors; six months alone at age 23 does not establish infertility requiring the same work-up.

records.question: During resuscitation, when is the given position indicated?
options: Unconsciousness with pulse and breathing absent
Unconsciousness with pulse present and breathing absent
Unconsciousness with pulse and breathing present
Unconsciousness with pulse absent and breathing present
records.explanation: An unresponsive person who is breathing normally may be positioned to help maintain the airway while breathing is monitored and help is obtained.

records.question: A 50-year-old woman presents with foul-smelling bloody discharge per vagina mixed with mucous. On examination, a necrotizing growth is seen in the cervix with lateral parametrium involvement. What is the management for this patient?
records.explanation: Parametrial involvement without pelvic-wall extension is consistent with stage IIB cervical cancer. Definitive chemoradiation is a standard approach for suitable patients, but full staging and specialist planning determine treatment.

records.question: A woman is set to undergo a complete laparoscopic hysterectomy. She wants to know if there are any disadvantages to this procedure. What are the disadvantages of laproscopis over-open surgery?
options: Not knowing the extent of thermal burns
records.explanation: Thermal injury can extend beyond the visible contact point and may present late because tissue necrosis evolves after surgery. Recognition depends on the energy device, anatomy and postoperative course rather than visible injury alone.

records.question: A 27-year-old pregnant G3P2L2 woman presents to you at 36+6 weeks. Ultrasound is done and shows the fetus is in a transverse lie. The liquor is adequate, the placenta is normal, and she has no risk factors. Both her previous deliveries were normal vaginal deliveries. How will you manage this patient?
records.explanation: External cephalic version may be considered near term for a non-cephalic singleton when there are no contraindications and emergency obstetric care is available. Eligibility depends on placentation, membranes, fetal status and other factors.

records.question: A female presents to you with 6 weeks of amenorrhea complaining of bleeding per vagina and slight abdominal pain. The urine pregnancy test is positive and hCG level is 2800 IU/L. A mass is seen on the left adnexa measuring 3 x 2.5 cm. She is hemodynamically stable. How will you manage this patient? hCG-Human chorionic gonadotropin
records.explanation: Methotrexate can treat selected haemodynamically stable unruptured ectopic pregnancies with reliable follow-up and suitable biochemical and ultrasound findings. A small mass and modest hCG support consideration but do not exclude contraindications or rupture risk.

records.question: A 24-year-old woman who is being treated for infertility with human menopausal gonadotropin came with complaints of sudden abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and breathlessness. The finding of the ultrasound is shown below. What is the most likely diagnosis?
records.explanation: Gonadotropin stimulation can produce ovarian enlargement and increased vascular permeability, causing ascites and other manifestations of ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome. The absent ultrasound prevents confirming the pictured ovarian findings.

records.question: During a hysteroscopic removal of a submucosal fibroid, a fluid deficit of 2000 mL is estimated in a patient. What is the immediate complication of this?
records.explanation: Excess absorption of hysteroscopic distension fluid can cause circulatory overload and pulmonary oedema. Hypotonic electrolyte-free fluids additionally risk hyponatraemia; safe deficit limits depend on the fluid and patient factors.

records.question: A woman comes with complaints of pain and swelling in the perineal area. She also has complaints of difficulty in walking and sitting. She gives a history of multiple sexual partners. On examination, a tender swelling is seen with redness on the labia, as shown in the image given below. What is the most likely diagnosis?
records.explanation: A tender swelling near the posterior vaginal introitus can represent a Bartholin gland abscess. Examination establishes the site, and management depends on drainage needs, recurrence and patient-specific factors.

records.question: A 54-year-old woman was diagnosed with advanced cervical cancer. She has a 14-year-old daughter. What advice would you give her daughter?
records.explanation: HPV vaccination before exposure reduces risk from vaccine-covered HPV types and is relevant to an adolescent daughter regardless of a mother's cervical cancer diagnosis. It prevents future infection-related disease and does not treat an existing cancer.

records.question: A 17-year-old girl is seen for primary amenorrhea. There is no development of breasts or hair in the pubic or axillary region. Her height is 155 cm, and her weight is 48 kg. She has bilateral inguinal masses. The uterus, fallopian tube, and Ovary are absent on ultrasound examination. What is the most likely diagnosis?
records.explanation: Absent Mullerian structures with inguinal gonads suggests testicular anti-Mullerian hormone activity in a 46,XY differential. Gonadotropins, sex-steroid measurements and genetic assessment distinguish androgen insensitivity from impaired hormone synthesis or gonadal function.

records.question: A 54-year-old woman presents with cervical cancer stage 2A. It is decided to give neoadjuvant chemotherapy. What does neoadjuvant chemotherapy mean?
options: Chemotherapy is given along with radiation.
Chemotherapy is given before radical surgery to reduce the bulk of the tumor
Chemotherapy is given after radical surgery for micrometastases
records.explanation: Neoadjuvant therapy is given before the main definitive treatment, often surgery. Knowing this definition does not itself establish that neoadjuvant chemotherapy is the preferred regimen for a particular cervical cancer stage.

records.question: A 16-year-old girl presents with cyclical pelvic pain every month. She has not achieved menarche yet. On examination, a suprapubic bulge can be seen in the lower abdomen. PR examination reveals a bulging swelling in the anterior aspect. What is the most likely diagnosis?
options: Transverse vaginal septum above the vagina
records.explanation: An imperforate hymen can obstruct menstrual outflow, causing primary amenorrhoea, cyclical pain and a bulging membrane from retained blood. Examination and imaging distinguish it from higher outflow-tract anomalies.

records.question: A pregnant woman comes to the clinic. She already has twins by normal delivery. Which of the following is the correct representation of her obstetric score?
records.explanation: Gravidity counts pregnancies, while parity counts qualifying birth events rather than the number of infants. A previous twin delivery contributes one parity event; a current second pregnancy therefore gives G2P1 under the stated convention.

records.question: A patient presents with sudden onset of hematemesis. He has been taking aspirin for his arthritis and drinks alcohol occasionally. He gives a history of occasional abdominal pain. On examination, there is no abdominal mass or tenderness. What is the likely diagnosis?
records.explanation: Aspirin impairs platelet function and gastric mucosal protection, increasing upper gastrointestinal bleeding risk, including from peptic ulcers. The bleeding source still requires evaluation rather than assumption from aspirin exposure alone.

records.question: A woman presents to you at 36 weeks of gestation with complaints of feeling lightheadedness and dizziness when she lies on her back. She says she feels alright if she lies on her side or when walks. What is the most likely reason behind this? IVC- inferior vena cava
options: Excessive venous pooling at the feet
records.explanation: In late pregnancy, the gravid uterus can compress the inferior vena cava in the supine position, reducing venous return and blood pressure. Lateral positioning or uterine displacement can improve venous return.

records.question: A 40-year-old male patient presents with a swelling that has been slowly growing in the past 2 years. On examination, it was variable in consistency and fully mobile. What is the most likely diagnosis?
records.explanation: A benign parotid tumour can present as a slowly enlarging, mobile swelling in the parotid region. Pleomorphic adenoma often has variable consistency because of its mixed tissue components.

records.question: A woman with endometrial carcinoma is undergoing radiotherapy. Which of the following is true?
options: Intensity is inversely proportional to the square of the distance from the source
Small blood vessels are most radioresistant
Rapidly proliferating cells are most radioresistant
Small intestinal mucosa is most radio-resistant
records.explanation: For an ideal point source without attenuation, intensity is inversely proportional to the square of distance. Doubling distance reduces intensity to one quarter; real geometry and shielding can alter this approximation.

records.question: A child before playing consumed fruit from the garden. After some time he developed a high fever, confusion, photophobia, and unable to urinate. What are the likely causative agent and the appropriate antidote used in this case?
records.explanation: Datura contains antimuscarinic alkaloids. Physostigmine can reverse selected severe central antimuscarinic toxicity, but its use requires monitored expert assessment and exclusion of important contraindications; it is not routine treatment for every delirious poisoning.

records.question: A patient presents with a history of fever and cough for the past 3-5 days. His examination findings reveal crepitations. Chest X-ray is given below. What is the probable diagnosis?
options: Apical segment of Right lower lobe consolidation
Posterior segment of right lower lobe consolidation
records.explanation: Right middle lobe consolidation can obscure the right heart border on a frontal chest radiograph.

records.question: Injury at which of the following marked sites causes failure of dorsiflexion?
records.explanation: The deep fibular nerve supplies principal ankle dorsiflexors, and a common fibular lesion can cause foot drop with additional eversion weakness.

records.question: A patient presents with swelling under the left ear lobule and complains of pain. Which of the following structures is the likely cause of the pain?
options: Investing layer of deep cervical fascia
records.explanation: The great auricular nerve, arising from C2-C3, supplies skin over the parotid region and part of the external ear including the lobule. It is a cervical plexus sensory nerve rather than a facial motor branch.

records.question: A child presents with bone pain and hepatosplenomegaly. A trephine biopsy and aspirate show the following finding. Which of the following is the most likely enzyme deficient in this condition?
records.explanation: Gaucher disease results from deficient lysosomal glucocerebrosidase activity and lipid-laden macrophages.

records.question: The method of autopsy carried out en masse to remove from tongue to prostate is.
records.explanation: The Letulle method removes thoracic, cervical, abdominal and pelvic organs as a combined block before dissection. It differs from removing organs individually or in separate functional blocks.

records.question: A 42-year-old HIV-positive patient died, and his body was brought for post-mortem. The method of autopsy to be done is___
records.explanation: Rokitansky dissection is largely performed in situ. HIV status alone does not mandate one universal eponymous autopsy technique; appropriate biosafety, sharps precautions and aerosol control apply regardless of the chosen method.

records.question: A patient presented with a high fever, altered sensorium, headache, neck rigidity, and seizures. He was diagnosed with HSV encephalitis. Which of the following tests can be used to confirm the diagnosis?
options: CSF culture on chick embryo lines
records.explanation: CSF PCR is an important test for herpes simplex encephalitis. An early negative result can be misleading, so repeat testing and continued empiric antiviral treatment may be appropriate when clinical suspicion remains high.

records.question: In a patient presented with a fever and a positive filarial antigen test, what is the next appropriate method of management?
options: Detection of microfilariae in the blood smear
records.explanation: Demonstrating microfilariae in blood can establish a filarial infection when sampling and species context are appropriate. A diagnostic test is not itself treatment; management requires identification and assessment of the relevant filarial disease.

records.question: A 10-year-old male child came to the casualty with difficulty in walking and pain in the perianal region. On subjecting the specimen from the perianal region to a test, it produces yellow needle-shaped rhombic crystals with picric acid. What is the test done?
records.explanation: The Barberio reaction is a historical crystal test associated with spermine in semen. Such a presumptive chemical test cannot alone prove sexual assault, consent, timing or the identity of a contributor.

records.question: Which of the following refractive errors is associated with the image given below?
records.explanation: Astigmatism means refractive power differs between meridians, preventing a single focal point.

records.question: Which of the following is true regarding the Mendelian mode of inheritance?
options: Every 10th patient has a Y-linked disorder
1/3rd of Mendelian disorders is autosomal recessive
Every 5th patient has an X-linked recessive disorder
2/3 rd of Mendelian disorders are autosomal dominant
records.explanation: A claim that roughly two thirds of catalogued Mendelian disorders are autosomal dominant depends on the catalogue, date and counting method. It is not a universal fraction of affected people, inherited disease burden or all genetic disorders.

records.question: A patient was brought to casualty with seizures. He had multiple episodes and was taking herbal medicines for the same. He was conscious in between the episodes. During the episodes, he had arching of his back. What is the likely cause?
records.explanation: Strychnine blocks inhibitory glycine receptors, causing painful stimulus-triggered muscle spasms with consciousness often initially preserved. These spasms differ mechanistically from typical cortical epileptic seizures.

records.question: An infant is brought with complaints of excessive watering of the eyes and photophobia. The image is given below. What is the likely diagnosis?
records.explanation: Congenital glaucoma can cause enlarged corneas, tearing, photophobia and corneal haze from raised intraocular pressure.

records.question: A 60-year-old patient complains of decreased distant vision but now he does not use spectacles for near vision. The image of his ocular examination is given below. What is this type of refractive error called?
records.explanation: Nuclear lens sclerosis can alter refractive index and produce a myopic shift, sometimes temporarily improving unaided near vision.

records.question: A child is brought to the hospital with respiratory distress and biphasic stridor. The radiograph is shown below. What is the diagnosis?
records.explanation: Croup commonly causes a barking cough and inspiratory stridor from subglottic inflammation. Biphasic stridor can indicate more fixed central airway narrowing, so atypical features warrant reassessment rather than automatic attribution to croup.

records.question: A child presents with intermittent jaundice and splenomegaly. There is a history of similar complaints in the elder brother. Peripheral smear shows the following finding. How will you investigate this condition?
records.explanation: Spherocytes are vulnerable to hypotonic lysis because of reduced membrane surface area relative to volume. Osmotic fragility can support hereditary spherocytosis but is not specific; other tests such as eosin-5-maleimide binding may clarify the diagnosis.

records.question: A 3-month-old baby presents with jaundice and clay-coloured stools. Lab investigation reveals that the baby has conjugated hyperbilirubinemia. The liver biopsy shows periductal proliferation. What is the most likely diagnosis?
records.explanation: Persistent jaundice with conjugated hyperbilirubinaemia and pale stools in an infant raises concern for biliary atresia. Prompt specialist evaluation matters because early diagnosis affects the opportunity for effective surgery.

records.question: Section 314 IPC deals with
options: Causing miscarriage with the consent of the mother
Causing miscarriage without the consent of the mother
Death of the mother by act done with intent to cause miscarriage
Causing the death of the quick unborn child by an act amounting to culpable homicide
records.explanation: The historical IPC provision addresses death caused by an act intended to induce miscarriage. The statutory question concerns that historical legal framework.

records.question: An African child is found to have a mass in the jaw. A biopsy of the mass was done, and it appears as shown in the image below. The child also had a translocation of t(8;14). What is the probable diagnosis?
records.explanation: The classic t(8;14) places MYC under immunoglobulin heavy-chain regulatory influence, driving proliferation in Burkitt lymphoma. Variant immunoglobulin light-chain translocations also occur.

records.question: An infant presents with hepatosplenomegaly and thrombocytopenia. Neuroimaging with CT shows periventricular calcifications. What is the most likely diagnosis?
records.explanation: Congenital CMV can cause periventricular calcification, microcephaly, hearing loss and thrombocytopenia. Appropriate virological sampling early in life distinguishes congenital from later-acquired infection.

records.question: The temperature of a body of a deceased person is found to be 39 degrees Celsius. Which of the following is the most probable reason?
records.explanation: Sepsis can be associated with a high temperature around death, but a single elevated postmortem measurement is not specific for sepsis. Premortem fever, environment and postmortem processes must be considered.

records.question: A 35-year-old homeless man presented with a 1-month history of fever, cough, and weight loss. Both sputum smears turned out to be negative, but the chest x-ray ordered was suggestive of tuberculosis. According to the recent NTEP guidelines, which is the next best line of management?
options: Wait until TB culture results to start ATT
records.explanation: A cartridge-based nucleic acid amplification test can detect Mycobacterium tuberculosis and selected resistance markers even when smear microscopy is negative. A negative result does not exclude every form of TB, and specimen quality and disease site matter.

records.question: A farmer was sleeping in the field, and he felt a sting on his leg. He saw something moving away quickly. He then got drowsy and was taken to the hospital. He developed pain around the site and continued to bleed profusely from the wound site. The wound became red with blisters. Which of the following is the most likely cause?
records.explanation: Local swelling with bleeding or coagulopathy can fit viper envenoming. A clinical syndrome does not reliably identify an exact snake species, and treatment depends on urgent clinical and coagulation assessment.

records.question: A patient was transfused 4 units of blood 2 hours ago, and now she complains of chest discomfort. X-ray shows bilateral fissural thickening. Which of the following is the most probable cause?
records.explanation: Respiratory deterioration after multiple transfusions with congestion and volume-overload findings supports TACO. TRALI and other causes of acute lung injury remain differentials; volume history and haemodynamic evidence help distinguish them.

records.question: Which of the following is the sensitive indicator to assess the availability, utilization, and effectiveness of healthcare in a community?
records.explanation: Infant mortality rate expresses deaths before the first birthday per 1,000 live births in a defined period. It reflects multiple social and health-system influences and is not a specific measure of healthcare quality alone.

records.question: A 5-year-old child is brought with fever, fatigue, and left ventricular dysfunction. An endomyocardial biopsy is shown below. What is the probable diagnosis?
records.explanation: Lymphocytic myocarditis features inflammatory infiltrates with associated myocyte injury on tissue assessment.

records.question: An elderly male went for a medical examination. Laboratory investigations showed a marked elevation of lymphocytes with marked leukocytosis. The peripheral smear of the patient is given below. What is the appropriate next step for this patient?
records.explanation: Flow cytometry identifies a clonal B-cell population and its immunophenotype when evaluating suspected chronic lymphocytic leukaemia. Smudge cells alone are not diagnostic, and the absolute clonal-cell count and clinical setting distinguish related entities.

records.question: A 25-year-old male presented with low hemoglobin, platelet count of 25,000/mL, gum bleeding, and raised PT & aPTT. The image of his peripheral smear is given below. What is the likely diagnosis?
records.explanation: The characteristic t(15;17) produces PML-RARA in acute promyelocytic leukaemia. Associated coagulopathy makes suspected disease an emergency requiring rapid specialist treatment rather than waiting passively for every confirmatory test.

records.question: A young patient presents with a large retroperitoneal hemorrhage. He also gives a frequent history of intermittent swelling of knees on strenuous exercise. There is no history of any mucosal bleeding. Which among the following clotting factors is responsible for the condition mentioned above?
records.explanation: Factor VIII and IX activity assays distinguish haemophilia A from haemophilia B. They are alternative factor deficiencies in typical cases, not an assumption that both factors are deficient together.

records.question: A chronic smoker who worked in a cement factory for 20 years developed mesothelioma. The association is likely to be due to ________.
records.explanation: Asbestos exposure increases the risk of malignant mesothelioma. Established asbestosis is not a prerequisite for mesothelioma, so the exposure association should not be restated as a requirement for pre-existing fibrotic lung disease.

records.question: The average daily dietary nutrient intake level sufficient to meet the nutrient requirements of nearly all (97-98%) healthy individuals in a particular life stage and gender group is known as?
records.explanation: An RDA is designed to meet the nutrient requirement of nearly all healthy people in a specified group, conventionally about 97-98 percent. The estimated average requirement instead corresponds to approximately half the group.

records.question: Which of the following is true regarding the image provided?
records.explanation: EMLA combines lidocaine and prilocaine. Prilocaine metabolites can oxidise haemoglobin and cause methaemoglobinaemia, particularly with excessive exposure or susceptible patients.

records.question: A patient presents with no pulse, and the ECG shows the following rhythm. What is the next appropriate step?
options: Defibrillate, check pulse and then perform CPR
Defibrillate, perform CPR, and then check the pulse
records.sourceAnswer: Defibrillate, perform CPR, and then check the pulse
records.explanation: Ventricular fibrillation or pulseless ventricular tachycardia requires defibrillation followed immediately by CPR. Routine pulse checking immediately after a shock delays compressions; rhythm and pulse reassessment follow the resuscitation algorithm.

records.question: Identify the arrow-marked nerve
records.explanation: The medial pectoral nerve usually arises from the medial cord and commonly pierces pectoralis minor before supplying the pectoral muscles. The operative image must establish the labelled nerve's course.

records.question: Behind the medial malleolus and in front of Achilles, which artery is present?
records.explanation: The posterior tibial artery passes behind the medial malleolus in the tarsal-tunnel region. This relationship explains the location used for palpating its pulse.

records.question: The covering of an omphalocele is derived from which layer?
records.explanation: An omphalocele has a covering sac including an outer amniotic layer and an inner peritoneal layer. Gastroschisis lacks this covering membrane and is usually adjacent to the umbilicus.

records.question: A patient presents with xanthomas on the Achilles tendon. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
records.explanation: Tendon xanthomas with markedly elevated LDL suggest familial hypercholesterolaemia. They reflect lipid deposition in tendons and differ from the chylomicronaemia pattern dominated by high triglycerides.

records.question: A patient with multiple tendon xanthomas is found to have a serum cholesterol level of 398 mg/dL and an LDL level of 220 mg/dL. What is the most likely defect?
records.explanation: Impaired LDL-receptor-mediated clearance is the classic mechanism of familial hypercholesterolaemia.

records.question: A 30-year-old patient presents with a history of flat lesions near the anal canal, rashes on the body, and hair loss that follows a particular pattern, as shown in the image. What is the diagnosis?
records.explanation: Secondary syphilis can produce a widespread rash, moist anogenital plaques and patchy moth-eaten alopecia. Serological testing and clinical assessment are needed to confirm the diagnosis and distinguish mimics.

records.question: A 38-year-old patient with hypopigmented nodular lesions with anesthesia overarm with ulnar nerve involvement underwent a biopsy and intradermal antigen test. Based on the image, which statement regarding the condition is most accurate?
options: Tuberculoid leprosy with a positive antigen test
Lepromatous leprosy with a positive antigen test
Erythema nodosum leprosum with a negative antigen test
Lepromatous leprosy with a negative antigen test
records.sourceAnswer: Lepromatous leprosy with a negative antigen test
records.explanation: Lepromatous disease has weak specific cell-mediated immunity and typically a negative lepromin test. Tuberculoid disease has stronger cellular immunity and more localised lesions with a usually positive test.

records.question: A singer is finding difficulty raising the pitch of her voice. On examination, her vocal cords were depressed and bowing. Which of the following muscles is involved?
records.explanation: The cricothyroid increases vocal-fold tension and length, helping raise pitch. Its external superior laryngeal nerve supply makes it clinically distinct from most other intrinsic laryngeal muscles.

records.question: A 45-year-old woman is diagnosed with right vestibular neuronitis. What findings are expected during the head impulse test in this patient?
options: When the head is turned to the left, the eyeballs move to the left with Nystagmus.
When the head is turned to the left, the eyeballs move to the right with nystagmus.
When the head is turned to the right, the eyeballs move to the left with Nystagmus.
When the head is turned to the right, the eyeballs move to the right with nystagmus.
records.sourceAnswer: When the head is turned to the right, the eyeballs move to the left with nystagmus. Forensic
records.explanation: With unilateral vestibular hypofunction, a rapid head turn toward the affected ear may be followed by a corrective saccade to regain fixation. The saccade direction and the failed vestibulo-ocular reflex must be distinguished from spontaneous nystagmus.

records.question: In medicolegal examination, the accused 18-year-old male claims he is 16 years old. Which joint x-ray should be done?
records.explanation: Epiphyseal maturation at several skeletal sites can contribute to adolescent age estimation. It has biological and population variability and must be interpreted with documentary evidence, examination and applicable legal guidance.

records.question: Police brought a person from the railway track with features of a dry, dilated pupil, dry skin , slurring of speech, and altered sensorium. The poisoning is?
records.explanation: Datura contains antimuscarinic alkaloids that can cause dry skin and mucosa, mydriasis, tachycardia and delirium. The combination of dryness and altered mental status distinguishes the classic pattern from an opioid toxidrome.

records.question: The flexion point in a ventouse delivery is located at which of the following positions on the fetal head?
options: 3 cm posterior to the anterior fontanelle
3 cm anterior to the posterior fontanelle
6 cm anterior to the posterior fontanelle
Midway between the anterior and posterior fontanelle
records.sourceAnswer: 3 cm anterior to the posterior fontanelle
records.explanation: The vacuum cup is centred over the flexion point on the sagittal suture, approximately three centimetres anterior to the posterior fontanelle. Correct placement promotes flexion and presentation of a smaller head diameter.

records.question: Identify the instrument shown below
records.explanation: Piper forceps are designed for delivery of the after-coming head in selected breech births. Their configuration helps accommodate the fetal body while applying traction to the head.

records.question: The patient is having a headache and confusion. A brain tumor diagnosis is made. Family history reveals brain and kidney tumors. Choose the correct option
records.explanation: Von Hippel-Lindau syndrome predisposes to CNS or retinal haemangioblastomas and renal lesions, including clear-cell carcinoma. A compatible family history can suggest this inherited tumour-predisposition syndrome.

records.question: A 62-year-old patient presents with left-sided arm and leg weakness, right-sided facial paralysis, and difficulty with horizontal eye movements. Based on the clinical presentation, which of the following syndromes is most consistent with these symptoms?
records.explanation: Ipsilateral facial weakness with contralateral limb weakness localises to the pons and can occur in Millard-Gubler syndrome. A conjugate horizontal-gaze palsy implicating the gaze centre favours Foville syndrome instead.

records.question: A patient presents with painful vesicles in the genital region. Identify the lesion shown in the image and choose the correct diagnosis
records.explanation: HSV commonly causes painful grouped genital vesicles or ulcers. Lesion nucleic-acid testing can confirm infection and help distinguish it from other causes of genital ulceration.

records.question: A 2-month-old child is brought to the ophthalmology OPD with the following presentation. What is the ideal management?
records.explanation: A visually significant infantile cataract requires prompt specialist assessment because deprivation can cause amblyopia. Timing depends on laterality, density, age and associated ocular findings.

records.question: A patient presents with a gradual loss of night vision and peripheral vision. What is the most likely diagnosis based on fundoscopy findings?
records.explanation: Progressive rod-predominant retinal degeneration causes night blindness and peripheral visual-field loss. Typical retinal findings support retinitis pigmentosa, while electrophysiology and genetic assessment may further characterise it.

records.question: A man presents with back pain following a road traffic accident. There was no history of neurological deficit. X-ray spine is done. What is the diagnosis?
records.explanation: An isolated spinous-process fracture is an injury to a posterior vertebral projection. A Chance injury is a flexion-distraction injury with different stability implications, so the fracture pattern must be assessed on appropriate imaging.

records.question: A child presents with growth failure. Biochemical analysis shows normal ca2+, normal PTH, reduced phosphate, and increased ALP. What is the diagnosis?
